2006-07

Robert Watkins (president)

12 entries

5 September 2006

Fifth SGA opened its year, swore in eight senators

At the first meeting of that year's Senate, called to order with 8 of 18 senators present, eight new senators were sworn in: Chris Anderson, Diane DeRosa-Reynolds, Leah Keys, Amanda Kidd, Suzie Moghaddam, Seth Norman, Tori Theiss and Christa Wilcox. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen reported $30,000 in organizational aid for the year, and the senate nominated committee heads and Judicial Council members, including Matt Holland as chief justice. The minutes record Jeanne L. Johnson delivering the executive vice president's report.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 5 Sep 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

24 October 2006

SGA tightened its budget after leaving $24,000 unspent

The Herald reported that SGA had left about $24,000 of its $115,000 budget unspent at the end of 2005-06, money that returned to Western's general fund. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen said SGA was cutting money from areas where it went unspent, adding almost $10,000 to organizational aid and $3,000 to the miscellaneous fund. Allen called the previous year a bad budgetary year but also a learning year.

In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2006 (Wayback)

25 October 2006

SGA-run referendum showed students favored the I-A football move

In an online referendum SGA arranged alongside the homecoming queen election, 64.6 percent of voting students, 1,095, supported WKU's proposed move to Division I-A football, with 600 against. A total of 2,136 students voted in the poll, and the 1,695 who answered the football question represented about 9 percent of enrollment. SGA President Rob Watkins, who held the student seat on the Board of Regents, said the poll would help him define a position but noted the homecoming tie-in likely drew football-friendly voters.

In the recordDaily News, 25 Oct 2006

2 November 2006

SGA senate unanimously passed a resolution backing the I-A move

SGA members unanimously passed a resolution saying they supported the move to Division I-A football, following the student referendum result. Watkins, as student regent and SGA president, still would not say what his own position was before the regents' vote.

In the recordHerald front page, 5 Nov 2006 (Wayback)

28 November 2006

Watkins resigned as SGA president and student regent

SGA's own senate minutes record that president and student regent Rob Watkins's resignation was formally read into the meeting at the senate's regularly scheduled Tuesday session, with senators told Jeanne Johnson would be sworn in as president at the Dec. 5 Winter Banquet. Senators had voiced concerns about Watkins at an unannounced 10 p.m. meeting the evening before. A Herald front-page account (Wayback, 2 Dec 2006) covered the same resignation but gave the date as 30 November; this entry follows the primary senate minutes, which date the reading of the resignation to 28 November, leaving students without representation on Western's governing board for at least a month.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

28 November 2006

Senate passed Books for Africa bill and a printing-quota resolution

At the same Nov. 28 meeting where Watkins's resignation was read into the record, the senate unanimously passed Bill 11-06-F, sponsored by Lucas Humble, to collect textbooks the university bookstore would not buy back and send them to Africa. Senators also unanimously passed Resolution 08-06-F, sponsored by Seth Norman, backing a university study of a computer-lab printing quota after administrators told SGA's Student Affairs committee how many pages some students were printing.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

28 November 2006

Senate heard Douglas Keen Hall was next for renovation

In a University Committees report to the senate, a member reported that the Student Life Foundation had discussed campus housing renovations and that Douglas Keen Hall would be the next residence hall to be renovated, within about three years. The same report covered a Budget Council discussion of rolling several student organizations' budgets, including SGA's, into the university's base budget.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

5 December 2006

Senate tabled two resolutions for lack of quorum at Winter Banquet meeting

With 16 of 31 senators present, the senate lacked quorum to act on Resolution 09-06-F on vending machine prices and Resolution 10-06-F on special events parking, so both were tabled. Executive Vice President was listed vacant, since Jeanne Johnson had moved into the presidency after Robert Watkins's resignation. The Judicial Council reported meeting on the time requirements for the student regent seat. Winners of the Outstanding Senator and Outstanding Committee Member awards, chosen by secret ballot, were announced later that evening at the Winter Banquet.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 5 Dec 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

27 January 2007

Fill-in SGA leader Jeanne Johnson challenged tuition plan at regents meeting

The Board of Regents approved a 7.8 percent tuition increase for 2007-08, bringing tuition and fees to $6,417 a year including the higher athletics fee. Jeanne Johnson, a junior economics and finance major from Marion described as a fill-in for the former SGA president, opposed the size of the increase for online and distance-learning courses, though she had no vote. She said 'We know tuition increases are inevitable' but argued distance learners should not carry that burden.

In the recordDaily News, 27 Jan 2007

February 2007

Johnson won the student regent election; SGA seated a full senate

Jeanne Johnson, SGA president and Marion junior, won the special election for Western's vacant student regent seat with 688 votes, 41 percent of ballots cast. The same Herald issue reported that SGA began the spring semester with its first full senate attendance since fall 2004.

In the recordHerald front page, 3 Feb 2007 (Wayback)

24 April 2007

Provost rejected plus/minus grading; Johnson credited SGA's campaign

Provost Barbara Burch told the University Senate she would not implement the plus/minus grading system the senate had passed 36-23 in March. SGA President Jeanne Johnson said she was grateful for the decision, noting SGA had raised awareness and led student protests, and pledged that students would keep fighting if the issue returned. She said 'I'm confident that the students' opinions have been expressed.'

In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2007 (Wayback)

2 May 2007

SGA banquet closed the year and swore in 2007-08 officers

At its annual banquet on May 1, SGA presented awards and swore in officers for 2007-08, with Jeanne Lynn Johnson of Marion becoming the new SGA president and student regent and receiving the Dero Downing Award. Johnathon Boles of Elizabethtown became executive vice president, Kayla Shelton speaker of the Student Senate, and Cherieth Lea Lineweaver administrative vice president. Amanda Beth Allen received the Charles A. Keown Award, SGA's highest honor.

In the recordWKU News, 2 May 2007 (Wayback)

2007-08

Jeanne Johnson (president)

15 entries · 47 index lines

13 September 2007

Fall senate election drew 25 candidates for 20 seats

SGA reported record interest in its fall senate election, with 25 students running for 20 available seats, the most applications President Jeanne Johnson said she had ever seen. Elections were set for Sept. 19 and 20 through TopNet, with an informational table in Downing University Center on Sept. 18. Public relations director Liz Goddard said more competition would produce harder workers.

In the recordHerald, 13 Sep 2007

2 October 2007

SGA co-sponsored mock gubernatorial election

SGA and the Office of the Secretary of State co-sponsored a mock gubernatorial election at Centennial Mall as part of Secretary of State Trey Grayson's Civic Literacy Initiative of Kentucky. The 127 students who voted chose challenger Steve Beshear over incumbent Gov. Ernie Fletcher, 74 to 50. President Jeanne Johnson and Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles called the event a success.

In the recordHerald, 2 Oct 2007

18 October 2007

Resolution demanded more state funding for Western

At its Oct. 9 meeting SGA passed a resolution asking the state government to appropriate more money to Western, which had received 54 percent of the funding the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended for fiscal year 2008. President Jeanne Johnson argued that tuition increases to cover the shortfall hurt students. The resolution stated Western needed the full recommended amount to meet its 2020 educational goals.

In the recordHerald, 18 Oct 2007

18 October 2007

SGA organized Walk Out Western budget protest

SGA sponsored Walk Out Western, asking students to leave class at 12:20 p.m. on Oct. 25 for a rally at the Colonnade to protest state budget cuts, with empty seats meant as a message to Frankfort legislators. President Gary Ransdell said he could not condone students walking out of class and doubted a single-campus protest would affect state funding. Johnson said other state universities declined to join but were watching how it worked at Western.

In the recordHerald, 18 Oct 2007

25 October 2007

Committee proposed $1,995 educational video subscription

SGA's Academic Affairs Committee, chaired by Drew Eclov, prepared legislation to buy a roughly $1,995 subscription to United Streaming, a Discovery Channel-owned site with about 45,000 educational video clips that Eclov called a version of YouTube for higher education. The committee planned to survey students and professors before bringing it to a vote. SGA also scheduled a vote on a resolution placing $1,000 in a field trip fund to support learning outside the classroom.

In the recordHerald, 25 Oct 2007

November 2007

Athletics director asked SGA for help on football attendance

Athletics Director Wood Selig came to the SGA meeting to ask senators for ideas on getting more students to football games as Western moved to the Football Bowl Subdivision, which required an average attendance of 15,000 to keep bowl eligibility. Senators suggested advertising on Western's website and Facebook rather than email, and later game times. Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles, who sat on a faculty advisory committee for athletics, arranged the consultation.

In the recordHerald, 1 Nov 2007

15 November 2007

SGA planned Listen Up Legislators lobbying campaign

SGA began laying groundwork for Listen Up Legislators, a spring lobbying campaign in which senators would meet legislators one-on-one in Frankfort to push for university funding, after the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended a $174 million increase for public universities. Chief of staff Skylar Jordan said the traditional February rally had not worked, pointing to Western receiving only 54 percent of the recommended increase. Other state student governments expressed interest in coordinating lobbying dates.

In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2007

31 January 2008

Spring session opened with ONE Campus bill

At its first spring meeting on Jan. 29, SGA introduced legislation by Senators Matt Vaughan and Doug Tate asking the senate to recognize Western as a ONE Campus, part of the national campaign against global AIDS and extreme poverty. SGA also released its spring schedule, including Listen Up Legislators on Feb. 14, the Frankfort rally for higher education on Feb. 20 and the annual banquet on April 29. In the semester's opening handout, Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles pointed members to the constitution's purpose of serving the student body equally.

In the recordHerald, 31 Jan 2008

20 February 2008

Fifty senators write down what a lobbying trip felt like

After a student rally at the Capitol in Frankfort, dozens of SGA members each filed an individual written reflection, archived one per person. The richest first-person source in the entire collection.

In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Frankfort rally reflections

April 2008

Spring election closed amid low-turnout criticism

Voting for three executive seats and 28 senate seats ended after a one-week campaign that candidates criticized as part of SGA's low-involvement problem; turnout had been 1,424 the year before and 1,376 the year before that. Red Towel Party presidential candidate Tedde Harden promised to rework what he called outdated election codes, while opponent Johnathon Boles agreed campaign time should be extended. President Jeanne Johnson said her administration inherited the codes and had tried new turnout methods, including extra credit for attending the debate.

In the recordHerald, 1 Apr 2008

17 April 2008campus

Ransdell announced 9 percent tuition increase

President Gary Ransdell announced at campus forums that he would recommend a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09, abandoning a plan to hold increases at 6 percent. The change followed a state budget crisis in which Gov. Steve Beshear ordered a 3 percent cut to postsecondary education in December 2007 and proposed an additional 12 percent, later reduced by the General Assembly to 3 percent. Ransdell said the swing from expected state revenue was about $11 million to $12 million.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2008

17 April 2008Other

Senator pushed WKU to join the Ruckus free music service

Kevin Smiley, senator and chair of the student affairs committee, wrote legislation asking administrators to apply for membership of Ruckus, a download service that let anyone with a .edu address stream music and films free from a company-supplied server. The senate was due to consider it on 22 April 2008. Smiley said the software was already available to students but could not run on WKU computers until the university joined, and that installing the server would cost the university nothing.

In the recordCollege Heights Herald 83:48, 17 Apr 2008 - "SGA bill pushes for free music" (TopSCHOLAR)

22 April 2008Service

Spring Oasis gave out exam supplies during finals week

On 22 April 2008 the senate voted $250 for Spring Oasis, then in its second year, a programme meant to relieve the cost of finals week. The money bought scantrons, exam books, pencils, pens and highlighters. SGA allocated a further $500 to provide refreshments for students in the library.

$250 for supplies plus $500 for library refreshments

In the recordCollege Heights Herald 83:50, 24 Apr 2008 - "SGA helps to relieve college expenses during finals week" (TopSCHOLAR)

24 April 2008

Student regent Johnson opposed scale of 9 percent tuition increase

The Board of Regents approved a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09 and finalized $2.5 million in cuts to the 2007-08 budget. Louisville regent Larry Zielke moved to cap the increase at 6 percent and push the General Assembly for more funding instead; SGA President and student regent Jeanne Johnson seconded the motion, but it died with only two votes. Johnson also argued the $370,000 budgeted for the Honors College should be reduced, saying the college benefited only 900 students and other students should not have to pay for it.

In the recordHerald 83:51, 29 Apr 2008 - "Regents approve 9 percent tuition increase, finalize 07-08 budget cuts"

18 July 2008

Johnson's regent term ended as Boles took the board oath

The Board of Regents read a resolution thanking Jeanne Johnson for her service as the board's student member from April 27, 2007 to July 18, 2008, calling her term one of "able leadership, faithful service, and dedication." Johnathon Boles, who had already been installed as SGA president that spring, took the oath of office as student regent the same day, formally completing the transition between administrations.

2008-09

Johnathon Boles (president) · Kayla Shelton (president) · Reagan Gilley (student regent)

14 entries · 41 index lines

4 September 2008campus

Shots fired outside Pearce-Ford Tower put dorms on lockdown

Campus police responded to a report of shots fired at about 3 a.m. Saturday in the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot, where a witness said a man got out of a vehicle, fired a gun and drove away. Police found shell casings but no damage, no one was hurt, and all dorms went into lockdown after the incident.

In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2008

18 September 2008

Fall senate election drew above-average turnout

SGA seated nine new student senators after a two-day fall election in which 18 candidates competed. Seven seats had been open, four reserved for freshmen, and two more opened when two senators resigned the Monday before the vote. A total of 687 students voted, which President Johnathon Boles said was higher than the average for a fall election.

In the recordHerald, 18 Sep 2008

13 November 2008

Boles and Smiley appointed to governor's college affordability group

Gov. Steve Beshear appointed SGA President Johnathon Boles and SGA member Kevin Smiley to the student committee of his College Access Work Group, which was charged with recommending ways to make Kentucky higher education more affordable. The two traveled to Frankfort for the committee's first meeting, where they raised the impact of textbook costs, which Boles put at an average of $800 a year.

In the recordDaily News, 13 Nov 2008

19 November 2008

Senate voted to launch a Textbook Subsidy Program

The SGA senate voted to contribute $500 to start a Textbook Subsidy Program, an effort developed with the University Bookstore, which pledged another $500, to build an endowment that would lower textbook costs for students. The senate also created a program board of nearly 20 members, including Boles, bookstore representatives and members from each college, to work out funding and distribution.

In the recordDaily News, 19 Nov 2008

4 December 2008

SGA made its first mid-year budget cut

Facing a state shortfall that required the university to cut about 4 percent of its budget, SGA cut $4,100 from its $110,000 budget, the first time it had cut its budget in the middle of an academic year. Boles and Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley chose to cut a $2,600 surplus from the fall retreat and $1,500 from organizational aid, protecting scholarships and Provide-A-Ride. Boles said he was working to get charter buses to send students to a Feb. 3 rally in Frankfort against higher education budget cuts.

In the recordHerald, 4 Dec 2008

29 January 2009campus

Ice storm hit campus, injuring a student and closing regional campuses

A winter storm coated campus in ice during the week of Jan. 27, part of the second-largest power outage recorded in Kentucky. A falling tree limb struck a sophomore near Grise Hall, who was treated and released, and WKU canceled classes at its Elizabethtown, Owensboro, Glasgow, Fort Knox and Radcliff campuses as well as evening classes on the main campus. AT&T cell outages kept officials from reaching students by text message.

In the recordHerald, 29 Jan 2009

12 February 2009

Judicial Council ordered a special student regent election over executive dissent

After Boles' resignation left the student regent seat empty, the SGA Judicial Council voted 2-1 on Feb. 10 to hold a special election on Feb. 24 and 25. Chief Justice Lisa Kappler cast the dissenting vote, calling the constitution's requirement a gray area, and Executive Vice President Skylar Jordan presented a letter arguing the election was unnecessary. President Kayla Shelton said she supported the council's decision.

In the recordHerald, 12 Feb 2009

12 February 2009

Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned

SGA Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned Thursday night in a letter sent to President Kayla Shelton and student activities director Charley Pride, saying she wanted to spend more time on school and family. Shelton said she hoped the senate would vote on a new chief justice at the next meeting because the special election for student regent was two weeks away.

In the recordHerald, 12 Feb 2009

24 February 2009Other

Senate refused an extra $82.27 for Reduce Your Use water bottles

A bill passed on 18 November 2008 had given Housing and Residence Life $650 to buy 420 water bottles as prizes for the Reduce Your Use contest, a competition between dorms to cut energy use and increase recycling, won by Minton Hall. When the bottles came in $82.27 over the quote, the senate voted nine to thirteen on 24 February 2009 against covering the difference. Administrative vice president Reagan Gilley said he had not wanted to take the money from the SGA budget without asking the senate.

$650 granted; a further $82.27 refused

In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2009 - "SGA denies money for HRL to purchase more water bottles" (Wayback)

26 February 2009

Reagan Gilley won the special student regent election

Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley, a Pineville senior, defeated Speaker of the Senate Nate Eaton 477 votes to 224 in the special election for student regent, with 701 students voting. The seat had been vacant for 26 days after former President Johnathon Boles resigned on Jan. 30 for health reasons; Executive Vice President Kayla Shelton had taken his place as president but not as regent.

In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2009

31 March 2009Programme

Organizational aid and $2,000 for The Come Up

At its meeting on 31 March 2009 the senate passed two bills awarding $9,029.04 in organizational aid to 21 student organizations. A third bill gave $2,000 to the Office of Diversity Programs for The Come Up, a programme to help black men build skills in academics, health and etiquette. The senate voted down a resolution urging WKU to enforce its existing campus smoking policy.

$9,029.04 in organizational aid to 21 groups; $2,000 to The Come Up

In the recordHerald, 31 Mar 2009 - "SGA awards org aid, announces another presidential candidate" (Wayback)

7 April 2009Programme

SGA put $500 into WKU's herb garden

On 7 April 2009 the senate passed a bill supporting WKU's herb garden, on the path between Downing University Center and South Lawn, giving the office of sustainability $500 to buy more varieties of plant. Recycling coordinator Cristin Lanham said the garden had been planted two years earlier so students, staff and faculty could pick herbs free, and that Fresh Food Company chefs sometimes cut from it. The garden was used to teach a workshop at the Campus Community Partnerships for Sustainability Conference that month.

$500 to the office of sustainability

16 April 2009

Kevin Smiley won the SGA presidential election

The Herald reported Kevin Smiley's win in the spring SGA presidential election under the headline "All Smiles, Kevin Smiley Wins Student Government Association Election," ending Kayla Shelton's term as the president who had finished out Johnathon Boles's 2008-09 year. Smiley took office as president and student regent for 2009-10.

In the recordCollege Heights Herald 84:46, 16 Apr 2009

23 April 2009

SGA negotiated removal of proposed $30 per-credit-hour fee

SGA and university officials agreed to strike a proposed $30 fee for every credit hour over 15 from the Board of Regents agenda, replacing it with a proposal to raise the add/drop fee from $20 to $50. SGA canceled a planned protest after the compromise, and Student Regent Reagan Gilley called the outcome "really a win-win for everyone."

2009-10

Kevin Smiley (president)

13 entries · 32 index lines

4 September 2009

Smiley nominates his brother as chief of staff

SGA President Kevin Smiley announced Danville sophomore Eric Smiley, his brother, as his nominee for chief of staff, a paid voting position on the executive cabinet. Former executive vice president Skylar Baker-Jordan called the nomination "completely unethical," while Smiley said he chose his brother because he had no previous political agenda. The senate was set to vote on all nominations Sept. 8, with a two-thirds majority needed for approval.

In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2009

15 September 2009

Fall election opens; SGA gives $2,000 to Residence Hall Association

At the Sept. 15 senate meeting, Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that SGA gave $2,000 from its budget to the Residence Hall Association. President Kevin Smiley announced that voting in the fall SGA election had started on TopNet, with polls open until Wednesday night and results announced about midnight. Smiley also urged senators to join the Campus Safety Walk, in which participants looked for dimly lit or overgrown areas on campus.

In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2009

29 September 2009Service

Provide-A-Ride was suspended and students started their own taxi

Parking and Transportation Services announced in September 2009 that Provide-A-Ride was suspended because the contract with Bowling Green Shuttle Service had ended. Three students, Zac Newton, Devon Hilderbrandt and Ryan Holland, set up Topper Taxi in the gap, charging $5 for one rider and $1 for each additional passenger. SGA administrative vice president Justin Thurman sat on the 18 September panel that reviewed bids from prospective providers, with a new operator due to be named on 1 October.

Topper Taxi charged $5 plus $1 per extra rider; Provide-A-Ride was free

In the recordHerald, 29 Sep 2009 - "Students give gas to taxi service" (Wayback)

14 October 2009

SGA sponsors forum on new tailgating policy

About 30 people attended an SGA-sponsored forum where students and administrators discussed Western's amended tailgating policy, which banned vehicles from campus lawns on game days. Howard Bailey, vice president for student affairs, told students the policy would stay the same, and Speaker of the Senate Wade Pierce suggested tent giveaways to ease the transition. President Kevin Smiley said he was pleased with the attendance and that SGA would keep questioning the policy.

In the recordHerald, 14 Oct 2009

20 October 2009

Three senators resign over publications committee appointment

Senators Michel Stephens, Emmett Stephens and Daniel Shaw resigned at the Oct. 20 meeting. Michel Stephens cited President Kevin Smiley's nomination of Greg Capillo to the Student Publications Committee, which helps choose the Herald's editor-in-chief, saying the pick was not based on merit or experience. Smiley called the accusations of favoritism and corruption unfounded and said the seats would stay vacant until he appointed replacements for senate approval.

In the recordHerald, 20 Oct 2009

10 November 2009

Judicial Council removes senator for unexcused absences

Chief Justice Stuart Kenderes reported that the Judicial Council removed Senator Theodore Harden, a graduate student from Otisville, N.Y., from SGA for excessive unexcused absences; Harden did not attend the council meeting to defend himself. The council also reviewed Senator Vashae Swope for absences but voted to let her remain. Attendance guidelines were posted in the SGA office window, and Rachel Wilcox was approved as a new senator at the same meeting.

In the recordHerald, 10 Nov 2009

11 December 2009

WKU begins weighing a smoke-free campus

After the University of Kentucky and the University of Louisville went smoke-free, the Faculty Welfare Committee of Western's University Senate prepared a smoking survey for students, faculty and staff to take in February. SGA President Kevin Smiley said he would encourage the whole campus to take the survey, and President Gary Ransdell said he would look to SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council for direction on any policy.

In the recordHerald, 11 Dec 2009

27 January 2010

Two more senators resign; Frankfort rally buses announced

At the Jan. 27 meeting, Aaron Pawley and Eileen Forsythe resigned as senators, Pawley because of a difficult course load and Forsythe because she was studying abroad in England. President Kevin Smiley announced free buses to carry 75 students to a Feb. 9 rally in Frankfort where advocates from Kentucky's public universities would lobby legislators on higher education funding. Western student Colton Jessie was slated to speak at the rally.

In the recordHerald, 27 Jan 2010

2 February 2010

SGA organizes trip to Rally for Higher Education

SGA and the Provost's office offered free bus transportation for 75 students to the Rally for Higher Education on Feb. 9 at the Kentucky State Capitol, a year after winter weather derailed the previous attempt. Students who registered through the SGA website received an excused absence, and the rally included a chance to meet lawmakers and hear an address from Gov. Steve Beshear.

In the recordHerald, 2 Feb 2010

22 February 2010

Senate passes funding bills for baseball, a sorority event and study abroad

At its Feb. 22 meeting the senate unanimously passed a funding bill and, with single dissents apiece, a bill funding the baseball program and a $1,300 allocation for an Alpha Kappa Alpha event. It also unanimously approved several study-abroad reimbursement bills and confirmed Daniel Shaw as parliamentarian, along with a new Academic Affairs committee chair nominee and a new Student Affairs chair.

In the recordSGA senate minutes, 22 Feb 2010

23 March 2010

SGA passes election codes and two funding bills

The senate passed the spring 2010 election codes, a bill giving $500 to the Agriculture Students Striving for Effective Tomorrows conference for high school students, and a bill designating $1,200 for lodging for FIJIs Across America, in which eight Phi Gamma Delta members planned to cycle across the country for Alzheimer's research. Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that all but three approved organizations had received their organizational aid checks.

In the recordHerald, 23 Mar 2010

April 2010

Colton Jessie elected SGA president for 2010-11

Bowling Green junior Colton Jessie won the SGA presidency with 63 percent of the vote, taking 726 votes to 424 for Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman, on a platform of sustainability, handicap accessibility and changing the tailgating policy. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president with 731 votes to Currie Martin's 415, and Wade Pierce ran unopposed for administrative vice president with 1,016 votes. Results were announced at midnight Wednesday.

In the recordHerald, 1 Apr 2010

4 May 2010Programme

Western T-shirt swap traded rival logos for WKU red

SGA sponsored a T-shirt swap during finals week of spring 2010, letting students trade in shirts carrying other universities' logos for a Western shirt at the SGA office in DUC 130. Student affairs committee head Emmy Woosley introduced the idea; executive vice president Kendrick Bryan said the collected shirts would go to a philanthropy, though which one had not been decided. SGA also planned an event near Java City in Helm Library during the extended library hours it paid for that week.

Colton Jessie (president)

10 September 2010Service

SGA listed its signature services, including Western Wednesdays

In a commentary published on 10 September 2010, executive vice president Kendrick Bryan set out SGA's standing services: organizational aid of more than $40,000 a year with up to $500 per group, Provide-A-Ride, study abroad scholarships and scholar development grants, free blue books and Scantron forms in the SGA office at DUC 130, and Western Wednesdays, a discount for students wearing WKU apparel honoured by thirteen restaurants. SGA was operating on a budget of $110,000.

$110,000 budget; more than $40,000 a year in organizational aid

In the recordHerald, 10 Sep 2010 - "LETTER TO THE EDITOR: SGA kick-starts new academic year at WKU"

10 September 2010Programme

The events the 2009-10 senate had helped pay for

The same commentary listed what the student senate had sponsored during 2009-10: FIJIs Across America, the American Collegiate Intramural Sports regional flag football tournament, the Wilson Family Endowment Fund for Injured Student Athletes, the mural near Schneider Hall, the Miss Black Western Pageant, the Rally for Higher Education and the Interfaith Dialogue on Earth Care. It is the clearest surviving inventory of a single year's SGA co-sponsorships from this period.

In the recordHerald, 10 Sep 2010 - "LETTER TO THE EDITOR: SGA kick-starts new academic year at WKU"

14 September 2010

SGA raised scholarship budget to $20,000

After running out of scholarship money the previous year, SGA increased its scholarship budget from $12,000 to $20,000 and lowered general senate funding from $20,000 to $12,000 to cover the change. Study abroad awards were capped at $500 for a semester trip and $250 for a winter or summer term so more students could receive money. SGA also finalized a new study away scholarship for travel inside the country and set aside $400 for it in the winter term.

In the recordHerald, 14 Sep 2010

SGA paid marketing students $885 for koozies and bottle openers

WKU's American Marketing Association partnered with SGA to market the organisation after AMA president Currie Martin, a former senator, argued that exposure was SGA's weakness. The senate passed a bill giving AMA $885 to buy 500 koozies and 500 keychain bottle openers carrying the SGA logo and the Provide-A-Ride phone number. President Colton Jessie called it a win for both sides, giving marketing students a real client.

$885 for 500 koozies and 500 keychain bottle openers

23 September 2010

Twelve senators elected in fall election with 847 voters

Twelve students won seats in the fall senate election, in which 847 total voters cast ballots on TopNet. Keyana Boka, Natalie Broderick and Eppiphanie Benton were elected freshman senators, running unopposed, while 25 students competed for the at-large seats. Winners included Diego Leal Ambriz, who would run for president that spring.

Campus Clean-up drew about 35 volunteers

More than 10,300 people had used it in 2007-08. No figures survived for 2008-09 because a fire at the Yellow Cab Company building destroyed the handwritten logs.

jointly paid for by SGA and Parking and Transportation Services

Free test forms switched to recycled Apperson sheets

SGA replaced the free Scantron answer forms it handed out in its office with 4,000 Apperson forms made from 100 per cent recycled material. $197 for 4,000 forms, against $300 for 1,000 Scantrons

Focus Fridays emailed the Greek presidents every week

SGA began Focus Fridays on 12 November 2010, sending Greek chapter presidents a weekly email with notes from the previous senate meeting and current business. Public relations chair Ann Blair Thornton said SGA had lacked relations with Greeks, who were often the most involved students on campus. 19 November 2010

Ransdell brought $49 million DUC renovation plan to SGA

President Gary Ransdell and head architect Jeff Stivers told SGA at its Nov. 16 meeting that officials were moving ahead on a plan to completely renovate Downing University Center at a cost of up to $49 million. Students would pay about $140 extra per year in fees for up to 20 years, and Ransdell promised students would be involved in every decision. SGA had to pass resolutions on the design and fees before the Board of Regents could approve the project.

7 December 2010

SGA funds extended library hours for finals week

The senate approved $600 to keep the library open until 2 a.m. during finals week, covering extra staff time and lighting. President Colton Jessie said continuing the service was never in question, calling finals "an important time for students."

7 December 2010Tradition

Second Dine with Decision Makers drew about fifty students

SGA held Dine with Decision Makers on 7 December 2010 in the Cupola Room, where Kentucky Secretary of State Trey Grayson and more than a dozen other officials shared tables with students. Bryan said about 50 students attended. Administrative vice president Wade Pierce, seated at Grayson's table, said the casual conversation showed him the secretary of state in a new light.

In the recordHerald, 8 Dec 2010 - "Students get to know decision makers at SGA event"

10 December 2010

Senate tabled DUC resolution over lack of student input

Senators tabled the bill supporting the DUC renovation at the Dec. 7 meeting, saying they had not received enough student input just three weeks after learning of the project. Jessie backed the delay, saying he wanted to hear students' voices before moving forward, even though it pushed SGA's presentation to the Board of Regents from January 21 to April 22. Campus Improvements Chair Kaylee Egerer said many students did not yet know they would pay $140 a year for the project.

4 February 2011Service

Provide-A-Ride outgrew its taxi contractor

By February 2011 President Colton Jessie said Provide-A-Ride had become too big for Franklin Taxi to run and students were waiting hours for a car. Between 31 August and 13 November 2010 the service carried 6,111 passengers on 1,189 calls, more than two-thirds of the whole previous year's total in three and a half months. Provide-A-Ride had carried 9,200 passengers on 1,772 calls across 2009-10.

11 February 2011

Herald reported Greeks held 40 percent of SGA seats

The Herald reported that 21 of SGA's 50 members belonged to Greek organizations, more than 40 percent, while less than 8 percent of the student body was in a fraternity or sorority. Sixteen of the 21 were fraternity men, and two fraternities, Sigma Chi and Lambda Chi Alpha, accounted for nine of them. Officers defended the imbalance, and the story noted SGA's operating budget for 2010-11 was $121,335, drawn from tuition.

SGA unanimously passed DUC renovation resolution

SGA unanimously passed the resolution supporting DUC renovations at its Feb. 22 meeting, the bill's second reading. Project costs were capped at $49,128,545, with a student fee of up to $70 per semester for 20 years and $1.5 million per year from WKU. The resolution, authored by Kaylee Egerer, asked for assurance of a 24-hour study space and called for construction to begin as soon as possible while interest rates were low.

In the recordHerald, 22 Feb 2011

SGA members joined Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort

SGA members traveled to Frankfort on March 1 for the annual Rally for Higher Education, where SGA secretary Katie Stillwell was the keynote speaker representing students statewide. Her speech urged legislators to protect money already set aside for higher education. Jessie, the previous year's keynote speaker, joined chief of staff Charlie Harris and other state SGA officers for a lunch with Gov. Steve Beshear.

Administrative Vice President Wade Pierce to hand post to fraternity brother

Pierce, who chaired the organizational aid committee, said he would be succeeded as administrative vice president by Devon Hilderbrandt, his committee co-chair and his "little brother" in Lambda Chi Alpha. Hilderbrandt ran unopposed in that spring's election.

Stephens won presidency with 56 percent of 1,066 votes

Billy Stephens, a junior from Hawesville, defeated senior Diego Leal Ambriz for SGA president, taking 56 percent of the 1,066 total votes in results announced just after midnight on April 7. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president and Devon Hilderbrandt won administrative vice president, both unopposed. All 35 senate candidates were elected to the 36 open seats, each needing just one vote to win.

Senate endorsed the Topper Talent Benefit Concert and funded One Planet Day

At its meeting on 12 April 2011 the senate approved $500 to buy reusable water bottles for One Planet Day, the renamed Earth Day observance, and passed a resolution endorsing Buck for Luck and the Topper Talent Benefit Concert, both run by Hilltoppers for a Cure and Relay for Life. Another $250 went to the National College Dodgeball Association national tournament. The last study abroad scholarship bill of the year gave $6,700 to 23 students.

6 May 2011

Senate tabled tobacco-free campus resolution

After nearly 45 minutes of debate, the senate tabled a resolution supporting a tobacco-free campus until the next semester. The resolution rested on a survey of more than 400 students in which 47.82 percent supported a ban, but senators argued the survey was biased because tombstones displaying the dangers of smoking had been laid outside DUC the day it was given. The campus improvements committee then said it would not support a ban until the two-year on-campus living requirement was removed.

2011-12

Billy Stephens (president)

42 entries · 50 index lines

6 September 2011

Senate reconvenes, appointments confirmed, tobacco vote postponed

At the semester's first senate meeting, held after the previous week's session was canceled, senators postponed a vote on the tobacco-free campus resolution so new members could review it first. President Billy Stephens made all of his executive-branch, judicial-committee and committee-chair appointments in a single blanket vote that passed unanimously, and Speaker of the Senate Kaylee Egerer told senators to keep generating new ideas for their committees.

In the recordHerald, 7 Sep 2011

14 September 2011

SGA ties tobacco ban support to ending two-year housing rule

The SGA senate passed a tobacco-free campus resolution that supported a ban only if the requirement for students to live on campus for two years was eliminated. Speaker of the Senate Kaylee Egerer said SGA backed the ban "if and only if" the housing requirement went. President Gary Ransdell had said the Board of Regents would not consider a tobacco-free campus until the University Senate, Staff Council and SGA each passed their own resolutions.

In the recordHerald, 14 Sep 2011

16 September 2011

SGA passes tobacco-free campus resolution with housing condition

The SGA senate voted unanimously for a resolution supporting a campus-wide tobacco ban, but only if WKU dropped its requirement that students live on campus for two years. President Gary Ransdell had said the Board of Regents would not consider a ban until SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council all passed resolutions. SGA was the only body to attach the housing stipulation.

In the recordHerald, 16 Sep 2011

21 September 2011

SGA waives its own process to oppose faculty regent term limits

SGA passed a resolution recommending that the Faculty Regent seat on the Board of Regents carry no term limit, following a University Senate recommendation the week before. The senate waived the usual two-week process of a first reading followed by a vote the next week. A bill funding the Cage the Elephant concert received its first read at the same meeting.

In the recordHerald, 21 Sep 2011

23 September 2011

Fall senate election fills 11 seats with 977 votes cast

SGA announced its fall senator election results just after midnight on Thursday, with 11 new senators elected including Christopher Costa, Corey Johnson and Mallory Treece. Twenty students ran for the seats and 977 students voted. President Billy Stephens said he was happy with the turnout for a fall election and that he got the contested race he wanted.

In the recordHerald, 23 Sep 2011

23 September 2011

Fall senate election draws 977 voters for 11 seats

Results of the fall senate election were announced just after midnight, with 11 senators elected from a field of 20 candidates. A total of 977 students voted. Those elected were Kelley Boothe, Hannah Garland, Corey Johnson, Elizabeth Wininger, Mallory Chaney, Mallory Treece, Kevin Asbery, Christopher Costa, Jordan Campbell, Nolan Miles and Ross Nowland.

In the recordHerald, 23 Sep 2011

27 September 2011Service

Free scantrons and blue books, a sponsored football game and a tailgate

At the meeting of 27 September 2011 SGA reported that free scantrons and blue books were now available in its office. It was sponsoring that Saturday's football game and an accompanying tailgating event for which students could register online, and it hosted a forum in DUC on the coming renovations from 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Campus Cleanup was set for 11 October with service credit offered.

In the recordHerald, 28 Sep 2011 - "SGA to host unveiling of DUC renovations"

30 September 2011

SGA to lend iPads through WKU's Educational Resource Center

SGA partnered with the Educational Resource Center in Gary Ransdell Hall to provide two first-generation iPads for the ERC to load textbooks onto and lend out to students at no cost, part of President Billy Stephens' push to make the organization more visibly useful to students.

In the recordHerald, 30 Sep 2011

30 September 2011

SGA spent $8,000 on Cage the Elephant concert, approving part of it afterward

SGA co-sponsored the Sept. 21 Cage the Elephant concert with the Campus Activities Board, splitting the costs. President Billy Stephens said the executive cabinet took $5,000 from executive discretionary money, which does not require senate approval, while a bill allocating a further $3,000 in senate funding passed on the Tuesday after the concert had already taken place. Stephens said there had been no rush for the funding because CAB had already covered the expenses up front.

In the recordHerald, 30 Sep 2011

5 October 2011

Ransdell tells SGA the two-year housing requirement cannot be dropped

In his first visit to SGA that semester, President Gary Ransdell told senators that eliminating the two-year on-campus housing requirement did not work "from a business standpoint." He said debts remained to be paid on dormitory renovations, so a certain number of students had to live in the dorms. SGA had been the only campus governing body to make removal of the housing requirement a condition of its tobacco ban resolution.

In the recordHerald, 5 Oct 2011

11 October 2011Tradition

Campus Clean-up ran during Make A Difference Week

Campus improvements chair Keyana Boka organised the Campus Clean-up for 11 October 2011, with service credit offered and gloves donated by the biology department. Seventeen senators volunteered alongside student athletes and a fraternity pledge class, and the group worked from Centennial Mall up the Hill to Cherry Hall and back to DUC. Boka said the clean-up ran twice a year, in Make A Difference Week each autumn and during Greek Week each spring.

In the recordHerald, 10 Oct 2011 - "WKU's SGA organizing Tuesday's Campus Clean-up"

22 October 2011Other

Croakies handed out at the Homecoming tailgate

SGA gave away croakies, straps that hold sunglasses round the neck, from its tent on South Lawn at Homecoming tailgating in October 2011. Administrative vice president Devon Hilderbrandt said the idea came from a summer retreat where members looked at what Kentucky and Eastern Kentucky handed out, and that croakies were cheaper than T-shirts or cups at about 75 cents each. The senate allocated up to $350 for roughly 250 of them.

up to $350 for about 250 croakies at about 75 cents each

In the recordHerald, 21 Oct 2011 - "SGA handing out croakies at WKU homecoming tailgating"

26 October 2011

Organizational aid bill passes for five student groups

SGA passed an organizational aid funding bill covering Black Men at Western, Women in Transition, the Western Kentucky Pre-Dental Society, Students in Free Enterprise and the Kentucky Public Health Association student chapter. A second aid bill received its first read, proposing $1,000 from the organizational aid fund for the Black Student Alliance and the WKU Habitat for Humanity campus chapter. Senators also discussed continuing work on Provide-A-Ride.

In the recordHerald, 26 Oct 2011

28 October 2011

Speaker says she never expects Regents to adopt SGA's tobacco ban version

Speaker of the Senate Kaylee Egerer said she did not expect the Board of Regents ever to enact SGA's version of the tobacco ban because the housing requirement was such a key factor. She said linking the two was necessary because requiring tobacco users to live on a tobacco-free campus was "infringing on students' rights." Egerer called the proposed ban "totally unfair and unrealistic."

In the recordHerald, 28 Oct 2011

9 November 2011

Senate defeats DUC name change resolution 19-8

A resolution to rename Downing University Center as Downing Student Union, written by campus improvements chair Keyana Boka, was voted down 19-8 with one abstention after a lengthy open debate. Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan suggested putting the question on the spring ballot, but senators noted architects working on the DUC renovation would need an answer sooner.

In the recordHerald, 9 Nov 2011

9 November 2011

Senate votes down renaming Downing University Center 19-8

A resolution that would have changed Downing University Center's name to Downing Student Union was defeated 19-8, with one senator abstaining. A motion to table the resolution was also voted down. Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan had suggested putting the question on the spring ballot as was done in 2006, but it was noted that architects would likely need an answer sooner.

In the recordHerald, 9 Nov 2011

15 November 2011

Herald editorial tells SGA to drop renaming and keep its promises

The Herald editorial board wrote that SGA should focus on student issues rather than renaming a building honoring former president Dero Downing, who had recently died. It said Stephens had barely addressed his platform promises, including a dead day before finals and an improved Provide-a-Ride service, which had seen no visible progress since SGA cut ties with Franklin Taxi.

In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2011

15 November 2011

Two senators removed for absences; ten faced judicial review

Ten of SGA's 36 senators were called before the judicial board during the fall semester for excessive absences from senate and committee meetings. Two of them, Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston, were dismissed from the senate after failing to attend their judicial hearings, which the council interpreted as intent to resign. The rest received warnings, and Stephens said he would appoint replacements to the two empty seats.

In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2011

15 November 2011

Ten of 36 senators face judicial review; two dismissed for absences

Ten of SGA's 36 senators were called before the judicial board that semester for excessive absences from committee and full senate meetings. Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston were dismissed after failing to attend their judicial hearings; Justice Chris Jankowski said each had between eight and 10 absences. Chief Justice David Spalding said the council interpreted not appearing at a review as intent to resign.

In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2011

18 November 2011

SGA pays surprise $15,000 bill for previous year's Provide-A-Ride

SGA paid Parking Services a $15,000 retroactive payment for the prior year's Provide-A-Ride service after Parking Services found no record of the previous administration's payment. The money was split evenly between the organizational aid and student scholarship funds, $7,500 from each. Stephens said he was "shocked" by the bill, while 2010-11 president Colton Jessie insisted his administration had budgeted the money.

In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2011

18 November 2011

SGA pays $15,000 retroactive Provide-A-Ride bill from aid and scholarship funds

SGA paid Parking Services a $15,000 retroactive payment for the previous year's Provide-A-Ride service, taking $7,500 each from the organizational aid and student scholarship funds. President Billy Stephens said he was "shocked" to be notified of the payment the week before, and that Parking Services had not received the money from the previous administration. Because the SGA budget does not roll over between years, no prior-year funds were available to cover it.

In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2011

24 November 2011Tradition

Thanksgiving dinner for students who stayed on campus

SGA and the Department of Housing and Residence Life co-sponsored a free Thanksgiving dinner on the 27th floor of Pearce-Ford Tower on 24 November 2011, open to PFT residents, international students, university police and anyone else left on campus. Attendance was expected at 50 to 60. SGA provided $220 for food and supplies; the funding bill gave the dinner an educational purpose, teaching international students about American Thanksgiving. It was the sixth year of the dinner and SGA's third as a co-sponsor.

$220 from SGA

In the recordHerald, 24 Nov 2011 - "SGA co-sponsors Thanksgiving dinner for those at WKU"

30 November 2011

SGA funds extended library hours and $2,500 in organizational aid

SGA passed a bill allocating $600 to Helm-Cravens Library to stay open until 2 a.m. from Sunday through Thursday of finals week, an annual practice. A second bill allocated $2,500 total to the Student Affairs Graduate Association, MBA Student Association, Topper Well, WKU Eco-Club, WKU Black Graduate Student Association and Kappa Alpha Psi. Three scholarship allocation bills received first reads.

In the recordHerald, 30 Nov 2011

December 2011Tradition

Third Dine with Decision Makers added the regents

SGA held its third Dine with Decision Makers on 1 December 2011 in the Cupola Room, free to students who booked online. President Billy Stephens said it was the first year the Board of Regents and university administration had been invited alongside legislators, and Gary Ransdell attended. Fourteen decision makers were confirmed, including the mayors of Glasgow, Owensboro and Elizabethtown, Warren County Judge Executive Mike Buchanon and Kentucky State Police Commissioner Rodney Brewer.

In the recordHerald, 2 Dec 2011 - "WKU administrators, government officials attend Dine with Decision Makers"

6 February 2012

SGA cancels $1,175 bus to Frankfort rally after eight sign up

SGA canceled the bus it had planned to run to the Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort, arranging carpools instead. As of that Friday only eight people had confirmed they were attending, and the bus would have cost $1,175, about $150 per student. The Tuesday night meeting, previously canceled for the rally, was reinstated.

In the recordHerald, 6 Feb 2012

7 February 2012

Herald editorial says SGA should and could do more

A Herald editorial said that after two short meetings and no new plans on the agenda, SGA appeared not to be on the ball, and urged it to do more before the semester ended. The editorial singled out the loss of the Provide-A-Ride service and the failure to find a replacement provider despite an offer from Parking and Transportation Services. SGA had said it would work toward a new service but admitted it was not feasible before the semester ended.

In the recordHerald, 7 Feb 2012

21 February 2012

Free speech resolution on student handbook delayed four weeks

A resolution supporting removal of the "External Computer Use and Ethics" section from the student handbook, which its backers said restricted freedom of speech, was scheduled for a second read. Its author, senator Christopher Costa, pushed it back four weeks to do additional research. The section warned that student posts on sites such as Facebook could be seen by university officials and that communications deemed inappropriate might lead to discipline.

In the recordHerald, 21 Feb 2012

24 February 2012

SGA approves $50,026 spring budget after $54,000 fall spending

The senate approved a spring 2012 budget of $50,026, divided among operations, public relations, executive programming and senate programming, with $10,500 set aside for organizational aid and $12,000 for scholarships. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell told senators SGA had spent about $54,000 in the fall, $15,000 of it the retroactive Provide-A-Ride payment.

In the recordHerald, 24 Feb 2012

24 February 2012

SGA approves $50,026 spring budget after $54,000 fall semester

SGA approved a spring 2012 budget of $50,026, of which $43,476.17 remained. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell said the organization had spent roughly $54,000 the previous fall, $15,000 of it the retroactive Provide-A-Ride payment. The budget was divided into operations, public relations, executive programming and senate programming, with $5,500 in stipends already spent.

In the recordHerald, 24 Feb 2012

29 February 2012

Senator removed for absences is reappointed by the president

Louisville sophomore Kevin Adams, removed from the senate the previous semester for excessive absences, returned through a presidential appointment by President Billy Stephens. Adams said he was less busy and had more time for SGA. Stephens said Adams had overbooked himself and that the two were good friends who had stayed close after the removal.

In the recordHerald, 29 Feb 2012

13 March 2012Other

SGA cancelled its meeting for an NCAA tournament viewing party

SGA called off its senate meeting on 13 March 2012 and instead hosted a free viewing of WKU's NCAA tournament game against Mississippi State in the Mass Media and Technology Hall Auditorium, with doors at 5 p.m. and food and drinks provided. Executive vice president Kendrick Bryan said SGA had first hoped to hand out tickets to the game in Dayton but distribution proved impossible because the tickets were sold through Ticketmaster at the University of Dayton. A second viewing was planned if WKU advanced.

In the recordHerald, 13 Mar 2012 - "SGA cancels Tuesday night meeting to host viewing party for NCAA game"

22 March 2012

Chief of staff resigns over grades; predecessor takes the job back

Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell announced her resignation at the Tuesday senate meeting, having officially resigned March 16. She said she stepped down because her grades were slipping ahead of a May graduation. President Billy Stephens named former chief of staff Eric Smiley as her replacement quickly enough that she did not need to serve out her two weeks' notice.

In the recordHerald, 22 Mar 2012

26 March 2012

Spring election postponed a day by TopNet failure

The spring election, set to run from March 27 to 28, was pushed back to March 28-29 because of campus-wide problems with TopNet. Director of Information Technology Cory Dodds said the election would slip another week if repairs were not finished in time. The executive cabinet made the decision with Charley Pride, director of student activities and organizations.

In the recordHerald, 26 Mar 2012

27 March 2012Festival

SGA co-sponsored International Night with $500

The senate passed a bill on 27 March 2012 giving $500 to International Night 2012, held free in DUC 224 on 19 April with food, a culture expo and a concert headlined by the Brazilian swing group Trio Ginga. SGA's co-sponsors were Downing University Center and the office of International Programs. Campus improvements chair Keyana Boka, a bill author, said supporting diversity was part of what SGA was.

$500

In the recordHerald, 10 Apr 2012 - "SGA co-sponsors International Night"

28 March 2012

Chief of Staff Eric Smiley approved after Stillwell's resignation

The senate approved President Billy Stephens' choice of Eric Smiley as chief of staff after Katie Stillwell resigned the post; Smiley had served as chief of staff two years earlier under his brother Kevin Smiley's administration. The same meeting passed five bills, including two Organizational Aid grants of $500 each to six campus groups (the Chinese Students and Scholars Association, Geology Club, Chinese Music Club, Relay for Life, International Club and Baptist Campus Ministry), $500 toward the April 19 International Night, $398 reimbursing two Kindle Fires raffled at the WKU Student Research Conference, and $500 toward Big Red's trip to the 2012 Mascot Nationals. Senators also passed a resolution for a second campus cleanup on April 17 and moved $3,000 from general senate funds to Organizational Aid so SGA could spend down its budget before the semester's end; announcements noted that spring executive elections would open at 12:01 a.m. the next day.

In the recordHerald, 28 Mar 2012

30 March 2012

Dodds elected SGA president for 2012-13; Boka and Alvey win uncontested VP races

Cory Dodds was elected SGA president for 2012-13 with 44 percent of the vote, over senator Corey Johnson with 35 percent and former senator Austin Wingate with 21 percent. Sophomore Keyana Boka was elected executive vice president and Cain Alvey administrative vice president; both vice-presidential races were uncontested.

In the recordHerald, 30 Mar 2012

17 April 2012Tradition

Campus Cleanup and Safety Walk on the same afternoon

SGA ran its spring Campus Cleanup from 4 to 5 p.m. on 17 April 2012 and held the Campus Safety Walk immediately after the senate meeting the same evening. Campus improvements chair Keyana Boka said the two were paired because neither took long. On the walk members noted dim areas and blue emergency lights that were not working.

In the recordHerald, 10 Apr 2012 - "SGA organizes events to improve campus"

17 April 2012Other

Senate gave $200 to Invisible Children after a fight over it

On 17 April 2012 the senate passed a bill allocating $200 to WKU's chapter of Invisible Children for its Cover the Night event, held that Friday at 9 p.m. in the Mass Media Auditorium to publicise the hunt for Joseph Kony. Several senators objected; Poorvie Patel was the first to challenge how the national campaign spent donations. The bill passed despite the debate.

$200

In the recordHerald, 18 Apr 2012 - "SGA awards $200 to WKU's Invisible Children after debate"

20 April 2012

SGA gave about $34,000 in organizational aid to roughly 50 groups

Administrative Vice President Devon Hilderbrandt said SGA distributed around $34,000 in organizational aid over the year, helping about 50 organizations. Groups applied online, met with the organizational aid committee, and could receive a maximum of $500 each. Senator Corey Johnson, who served on the committee, said the committee had been strict about what it funded.

In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2012

25 April 2012

Transgender inclusion resolution tabled after debate

A resolution by senator Kevin Asbery supporting policies more inclusive of transgender and gender-nonconforming students was tabled after debate. The resolution would have encouraged the university and its departments to revise policies and stated that WKU lacked adequate gender-neutral facilities, including housing and restrooms. Asbery said the issue had recently been brought to his attention.

In the recordHerald, 25 Apr 2012

2 May 2012

Transgender resolution passes 18-5 at final meeting of the year

At the last meeting of the year the senate passed the transgender and gender-nonconforming support resolution 18-5, with four senators abstaining. The resolution encouraged WKU to create gender-neutral housing and restrooms in all university buildings and to revise policies to be more inclusive. Students who were not SGA members attended specifically to watch the vote, and debate covered student safety, cost and whether separate housing would isolate students.

In the recordHerald, 2 May 2012

7 May 2012

Safe ride program finalized to replace Provide-A-Ride

President-elect Cory Dodds said SGA had finalized a partnership with Parking and Transportation to run a safe ride program in the fall, after a year without one. SGA's share would cost $15,000 for the school year, the same as under Provide-A-Ride. The earlier service had been a $30,000 contract split with Parking Services until original provider Franklin Taxi ceased its affiliation with WKU.

In the recordHerald, 7 May 2012
