2012-13

Cory Dodds (president)

39 entries · 31 index lines

6 September 2012

Senate unanimously opposed the bi-term and per-credit-hour tuition proposal

SGA unanimously passed a resolution opposing an administration proposal to emphasize bi-term courses and shift tuition to a per-credit-hour model. Dodds argued the change would charge students more, since full-time students then paid for 12 hours but could enroll in up to 18. He called it a financial burden students should not have to bear.

In the recordHerald, 6 Sep 2012

6 September 2012

SGA resolution opposes bi-term calendar and per-credit-hour tuition

The Tuesday meeting centered on a resolution opposing the administration's bi-term proposal, which would have put students in 80-minute classes on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays. President Gary Ransdell had said the change would let students take a full load plus a summer or winter course and graduate in three years. President Cory Dodds objected chiefly to the companion shift to per-credit-hour tuition, which he said would charge students more.

In the recordHerald, 6 Sep 2012

12 September 2012

Senate creates a long-term goals committee by executive action

SGA voted unanimously on an executive action establishing a special long-term goals committee of at least eight members, including students from outside SGA appointed by President Cory Dodds. Dodds said the committee could draw up a set of goals to focus on for the next few years. A bill to distribute $800 in senate funding as eight $100 Study Away scholarships received its first read.

In the recordHerald, 12 Sep 2012

25 September 2012

Fall senate seats filled after two resignations

Two senators resigned over time commitments and student Shea Wyatt was named to fill in. New freshman senators Barrett Greenwell, Taylor Ruby, Cole McDowell and Paige Settles were sworn in along with Gatton Academy senator Linda Cruz and graduate senators Mark Reeves and Katie Martin.

In the recordHerald, 27 Sep 2012

26 September 2012

ID voucher pilot program introduced covering 80 student IDs

A bill in first read would have SGA pay $10 toward each regular-priced student identification card under an identification voucher pilot program, partially covering the cost of 80 cards. A second bill sought $225 for the Sigma Gamma Rho sorority's Hair Show Spectacular. A resolution setting the fall campus clean-up date was held over because it had not reached the Legislative Research Committee.

In the recordHerald, 26 Sep 2012

9 October 2012Tradition

Senate bought T-shirts for the autumn Campus Clean-up

The senate unanimously approved funding on 9 October 2012 for promotional T-shirts for volunteers at the Campus Clean-up on 23 October, timed with Make a Difference Day. Committee chairman Mallory Chaney said dark grey shirts with the SGA logo would read something like "Tops making a difference" and would give students an incentive to turn out. Executive vice president Keyana Boka called the twice-yearly clean-up an important tradition, one the Herald traced back to WKU president Henry Cherry.

In the recordHerald, 12 Oct 2012 - "SGA bill funds Campus Clean-up"

17 October 2012

SGA adopts a new voting system and holds the South Campus food court resolution

At its eighth meeting SGA implemented a new voting system and gave a first read to an organizational aid bill covering the Student Veteran's Alliance ($175), the WKU chapter of the American Society for Microbiology ($150) and the Academic Competition Club ($275). A resolution supporting a food court at South Campus, due for a second read, was instead held in new business.

In the recordHerald, 17 Oct 2012

22 October 2012Tradition

Picnic with the president in the Ransdells' back garden

Gary and Julie Ransdell hosted SGA's executive board, student senators and the WKU Administrative Council for a cookout at their home on 22 October 2012, business casual. Ransdell said he had come up with the idea after months of talks with SGA president Cory Dodds about connecting his office to SGA. Dodds said the picnic had been running for several years and was an SGA tradition.

In the recordHerald, 17 Oct 2012 - "Picnic with the president a SGA tradition"

13 November 2012

SGA worked to restart a student government for the Glasgow campus

SGA officials traveled to WKU's Glasgow campus to help restart its dormant student representative body and connect it to main campus. Dodds said Glasgow students had no mechanism for their voices to be heard except contacting main-campus SGA. Roy Ratliff, nominated interim president of the Glasgow student body, said its top priority was establishing a writing center, for which the group had set aside $2,700.

In the recordHerald, 13 Nov 2012

14 November 2012

Senate reviewed its budget and heard a retention pitch

Speaker of the Senate Christopher Costa opened the floor to Joelle Carter, assistant vice president for Retention and Student Services, who asked senators for ideas on keeping students enrolled to graduation, and SGA's current budget balance was distributed to members.

In the recordHerald, 14 Nov 2012

14 November 2012

Retention official addresses SGA and gets no senator feedback

Joelle Carter, assistant vice president for retention and student services, spoke to SGA about keeping students enrolled through graduation and asked what student leaders could do to help. No senators offered feedback during the meeting, and she encouraged members to contact her later. SGA's current budget was circulated at the start of the meeting showing the remaining balance and money spent.

In the recordHerald, 14 Nov 2012

30 November 2012

Glasgow campus ratifies its own student government constitution

Glasgow's Associated Student Body ratified its constitution on Nov. 16 by unanimous vote with no abstentions. Interim president Roy Ratliff said the goal was to give SGA a presence on the regional campus and give regional students a vote in student government. The Glasgow body adopted the same bylaws as SGA and began selecting committees for the spring.

In the recordHerald, 30 Nov 2012

30 November 2012Service

iPad lending programme opened with the Educational Resources Center

SGA and the Educational Resources Center launched an iPad-lending programme giving students, staff and faculty access to tablets loaded with test preparation applications such as MCAT materials. ERC coordinator Roxanne Spencer said SGA had approached the centre wanting the iPads available for a pilot project. Executive vice president Keyana Boka said SGA had bought the iPads the previous year but could not start lending until they were secured against tampering.

In the recordHerald, 30 Nov 2012 - "SGA, ERC collaborate for iPad program"

5 December 2012

Provost pitches value-added grading to SGA at final fall meeting

Provost Gordon Emslie and University Senate member Guy Jordan addressed SGA on a proposed value-added grading system under which students in the top third of B and C grades would receive an extra quality point and a plus designation. Emslie said an earlier plus-minus proposal had taken several years to develop "only to be dashed at the last minute." Jordan argued the value-added version worked because faculty gave something up and students did not.

In the recordHerald, 5 Dec 2012

5 December 2012Tradition

Dine with Decision Makers moved to the Kentucky Museum

SGA held Dine with Decision Makers at the Kentucky Museum on 5 December 2012, seating officials from across Kentucky and WKU administrators at tables matched to students by interest or field. President Cory Dodds opened the evening and executive vice president Keyana Boka said the prayer. Wadsworth, Ohio senior Sarah Brazier gave the keynote, arguing that higher education built a productive economy and an informed citizenry rather than only advancing individuals.

In the recordHerald, 6 Dec 2012 - "Dine with Decision Makers"

8 February 2013

Senate rejects the value-added grading resolution in a close vote

The value-added grading resolution failed on a close vote, disappointing President Cory Dodds, who called it a tangible benefit that increased student competitiveness and said it was "a real shame that our senate didn't see that." Provost Gordon Emslie had introduced the system to SGA and the University Senate in fall 2012. Some senate members opposed the change.

In the recordHerald, 8 Feb 2013

8 February 2013Service

Safe Rides purple line returned for the spring

SGA's Safe Rides service, known on campus as the purple line, continued into spring 2013 after autumn 2012 became the first semester WKU ran a fixed-route late-night bus rather than a taxi contract. President Cory Dodds said the consistency of set pick-up points and times was why it worked where Provide-A-Ride had not. Administrative vice president Cain Alvey said Provide-A-Ride had been an unreliable taxi service by comparison.

In the recordHerald, 8 Feb 2013 - "SGA's safe rides program will continue for the spring semester"

12 February 2013Service

ID voucher programme halved the cost of a replacement card

SGA's ID voucher programme, running since the middle of the autumn 2012 semester, let students pay $10 rather than $20 for their first replacement student ID. The bill behind it allocated $800 to part-cover 80 cards. Administrative vice president Cain Alvey said the idea came from his job as a resident assistant in McCormack Hall, and that SGA covered only the first loss so as to teach responsibility and spread the benefit. Vouchers were collected from the SGA office in Cravens Library room 13.

$800 covering 80 cards at $10 each

In the recordHerald, 12 Feb 2013 - "SGA provides vouchers to replace lost IDs"

12 February 2013Programme

Eight Study Away scholarships funded as transcript vouchers ran on

The senate passed a bill on 12 February 2013 allocating $800 for eight $100 Study Away scholarships covering the spring and summer 2013 programmes. SGA reported that 30 of the semester's transcript vouchers had been used, with 70 left. Campus improvements chair Mallory Chaney set the spring Campus Safety Walk for 26 February.

$800 in eight $100 scholarships

In the recordHerald, 13 Feb 2013 - "SGA approves bill for Study Away scholarships"

15 February 2013

SGA passed its teaching assistant evaluation resolution

On Feb. 5 the senate passed a resolution creating teaching assistant evaluations, a program Dodds had campaigned on and drafted with his executive officers to pitch to Provost Gordon Emslie. Nicki Seay, chair of the Legislative Research Committee, wrote the bill, which aimed to make TA evaluation uniform across departments. The resolution next needed review by the Academic Quality Committee and approval by the University Senate.

In the recordHerald, 15 Feb 2013

15 February 2013

Teaching assistant evaluation resolution clears the senate

The senate passed a resolution for teaching assistant evaluations on Feb. 5, a proposal President Cory Dodds had campaigned on and developed with the executive officers before pitching it to Provost Gordon Emslie. The resolution next had to be reviewed by the Academic Quality Committee and, if endorsed, approved by the University Senate. Dodds said the idea had been worked on for many years.

In the recordHerald, 15 Feb 2013

20 February 2013

Senate tabled a plus-minus grading resolution

Senator Hannah Garland's resolution to adopt plus and minus grades for high and low letter grades was tabled after public relations chair Mac Mullins argued for a more formal proposal and more student input first; a similar plan had drawn SGA resistance when the provost proposed it in 2007.

In the recordHerald, 21 Feb 2013

26 February 2013

Senate amended the constitution, adding regional-campus seats

After two to three years of executive discussion, the senate passed most of a package of constitutional amendments, replacing class-year senate seats with college-based representation and guaranteeing seats for regional campuses such as Glasgow and Owensboro. A bylaw that would have made SGA members permanently ineligible for SGA-sponsored scholarships was stripped out and did not pass.

In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2013

26 February 2013

Plus-minus grading resolution tabled with a student ballot floated

SGA tabled a resolution for a plus-minus grading system that would add plus and minus grades to As, Bs, Cs and Ds. Author Hannah Garland, chair of the Academic Affairs committee, said the system would make GPAs more exact and might make WKU more competitive. President Cory Dodds said the executive board had discussed putting the question directly to students on the spring ballot.

In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2013

March 2013

Provost Emslie cancelled the bi-term proposal SGA had opposed

Provost Gordon Emslie announced at the Feb. 21 University Senate meeting that he was dropping his bi-term emphasis proposal and had no plans to revive it, citing input from students and faculty. Both SGA and the University Senate had passed resolutions against it. Dodds said the revocation was in the student body's best interest, saying "I strongly opposed it."

In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2013

March 2013

Constitution overhaul passes but senate strips the scholarship conflict rule

SGA adopted a package of constitutional and bylaw amendments with one exception: the senate rejected the bylaw that would have made serving SGA members ineligible for SGA-sponsored scholarships. Administrative Vice President Cain Alvey said executives had been discussing changes for two to three years and had gone through the constitution article by article, first presenting the changes on Feb. 19. Alvey said an amendment guaranteeing representation for regional campuses such as Glasgow and Owensboro was the one he liked most.

In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2013

March 2013

Four SGA leaders publicly accuse the senate of rejecting accountability

President Cory Dodds, Travis Taylor, Brittany Crowley and Drew Mitchell wrote a commentary attacking the senate for rejecting the amendment that would have barred serving SGA members from SGA-sponsored scholarships and grants. They wrote that 11 SGA members had received such scholarships or grants since the spring of 2011. The authors said this amounted to a breach of student trust and a conflict of interest.

In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2013

19 March 2013

SGA passed a resolution opposing the $150 Study Abroad application fee

The senate passed a resolution opposing a new $150 application fee for Study Abroad and Global Learning, set to begin with summer 2013 programs, arguing it could put program costs out of reach; the University Senate passed a similar resolution. A separate amendment proposed by Dodds to make SGA members ineligible for SGA-awarded Study Abroad scholarships failed. Dodds said 11 of the 125 such scholarships and grants that year had gone to SGA members, which he called a conflict of interest.

In the recordHerald, 19 Mar 2013

19 March 2013

SGA opposes the new $150 study abroad application fee

SGA passed a resolution opposing the $150 Study Abroad and Global Learning application fee, which was to begin with summer 2013 programs. Executive Vice President Keyana Boka said SGA took a formal stance because the fee had come up so suddenly. The University Senate had also passed a resolution against the fee, seeking to delay it until fall 2013.

In the recordHerald, 19 Mar 2013

27 March 2013

Executive candidates debate ahead of spring election

Outgoing President Cory Dodds opened a candidates' debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium by describing to the audience how much influence the students elected to SGA's executive positions would actually have on WKU's campus, ahead of the election that would choose his successor.

In the recordHerald, 29 Mar 2013

4 April 2013

Boka, Reeves and Seay won the spring executive elections

Executive vice president Keyana Boka was elected 2013-14 SGA president with 626 votes, 47 percent, over administrative vice president Cain Alvey with 419 votes and Austin Wingate with 300. Mark Reeves won executive vice president with 632 votes, 57 percent, over Brad Cockrel, and Nicki Seay ran unopposed for administrative vice president. Twenty-six student senators were also elected.

In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2013

9 April 2013

Judicial Council disqualified president-elect Boka, 3-2

In an emergency meeting, SGA's Judicial Council voted 3-2 to disqualify president-elect Keyana Boka after runner-up and outgoing administrative vice president Cain Alvey complained that a self-promotional email had gone to Honors College students at Boka's request, sent by Honors College graduate assistant Destiny Savage, violating the election code. The disqualification would have made Alvey, who had placed second in the April 4 vote, the incoming president; Boka said she would appeal.

In the recordHerald, 9 Apr 2013

9 April 2013

Regents committee approves SGA's teaching assistant evaluation policy

SGA announced that the Board of Regents had unanimously approved the teaching assistant evaluation resolution at its March 29 committee meeting, with the full board to take it up on April 26. President Gary Ransdell said he had recommended approval and that there was little discussion because students and faculty were in agreement. The policy would require departments to provide a way for students to evaluate teaching assistants.

In the recordHerald, 9 Apr 2013

16 April 2013

Judicial Council declined to contest Bailey's reinstatement of Boka

In an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council unanimously decided not to challenge Bailey's memorandum reinstating Boka, saying it did not believe it had the power to do so, while expressing official disapproval. Chief Justice Seth Church called the intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and said it set a bad precedent. Boka said the council had conflicts of interest and needed to be held accountable by a neutral party in the administration.

In the recordHerald, 16 Apr 2013

16 April 2013

Costa stepped down as speaker; Settles elected to succeed him

Christopher Costa did not seek another term as speaker of the senate, and senators elected Paige Settles to replace him. The same meeting confirmed presidential appointments Roy Ratliff as senator-at-large and Jackie Stewart as associate justice, with Chief of Staff Travis Taylor and public relations chair Mac Mullins giving reports.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2013

25 April 2013

Senate opposed automatic athletic-fee increases ahead of C-USA move

The senate passed a resolution against the annual automatic increase in the student athletic fee, arguing the revenue-sharing WKU would gain on joining Conference USA that July would outweigh the roughly $40,000 the university lost annually in the Sun Belt. Executive vice president-elect Mark Reeves, who introduced it, said the resolution set a precedent against automatic fee increases generally.

In the recordHerald, 26 Apr 2013

26 April 2013

SGA votes to end the automatic annual athletic fee increase

The senate passed a resolution supporting an end to the automatic annual increase in the student athletic fee once WKU joined Conference USA on July 1, 2014. Senator and executive vice president-elect Mark Reeves, who initiated it, argued that increased revenues made the automatic increase unnecessary. The resolution stated that WKU athletics paid $80,000 in the Sun Belt Conference but received only $40,000 back in revenue sharing.

In the recordHerald, 26 Apr 2013

10 May 2013

Budget cuts strip SGA's automatic inflation increase

University budget cuts announced that week removed the automatic increases that SGA, the Campus Activities Board and leadership programs normally received under the Higher Education Price Index, saving the university $8,000. Charley Pride, director of Student Activities and SGA's adviser, said no money was taken away, which was better than losing money. Incoming President Keyana Boka said the loss could affect new programs SGA had wanted to start.

In the recordHerald, 10 May 2013

4 July 2013

Former officer defends SGA's stance as administrators rename DUC anyway

Former Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan wrote after the Administrative Council decided the building would be called Downing Student Union. He wrote that former President Cory Dodds had correctly told campus officials students preferred Downing University Center, noting the student assembly had voted against the change in 2011 when asked to do so by administrators. Bryan wrote that student opinion had not changed since that vote.

In the recordHerald, 4 Jul 2013

2013-14

Keyanna Boka (president)

38 entries · 37 index lines

28 March 2013

Presidential debate drew full field of candidates

Ahead of the spring 2013 election, outgoing president Cory Dodds opened a debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium among presidential candidates Cain Alvey, Keyana Boka and Austin Wingate, plus executive vice presidential candidates Brad Cockrel and Mark Reeves and administrative vice presidential candidate Nicki Seay. Boka said SGA members needed better training in their roles, Alvey said the presidency's responsibilities went beyond the constitution, and Wingate, a former Speaker of the Senate, called for better representation across student groups.

In the recordHerald, 28 Mar 2013

3 September 2013

Judicial Council strikes down the international senate seat amendment

SGA announced that the Judicial Council had ruled unconstitutional a constitutional amendment proposed by President Keyana Boka and Executive Vice President Mark Reeves. The amendment would have changed the senate's composition by adding one seat for an international student. The ruling was reported to the senate at its second meeting of the semester.

In the recordHerald, 3 Sep 2013

6 September 2013

Emergency Judicial Council meeting clears reworded international seat

SGA called an emergency Judicial Council meeting to review revisions to the amendment the council had rejected on Aug. 29 for violating WKU's non-discrimination clause. Boka and Reeves changed the wording from "one international student senator" to a Navitas or English as a Second Language international student seat. Boka said the emergency session was routine protocol for any meeting outside the council's regular schedule.

In the recordHerald, 6 Sep 2013

10 September 2013

Executive Council floated plus/minus grading, set fall calendar

At the Executive Council's weekly meeting, Executive Vice President Mark Reeves reported that the University Senate Council had discussed reviving a plus/minus grading system and that Provost Gordon Emslie was interested in SGA's support. The council set a Nov. 9 Picnic with the President for the presidents' council and deans, and swore in Samantha Johnson to an executive cabinet seat vacated by the resignation of Keith Watson.

In the recordSGA Executive Council minutes, 10 Sep 2013

10 September 2013

Herald editorial questions SGA's handpicked approach to diversity

A Herald editorial examined the proposed permanent senate seat for an international student, ruled unconstitutional on Aug. 29 and then revised and approved in a six-minute emergency meeting. The editorial said it supported SGA's effort to expand representation but questioned whether a designated seat was the most effective means. Boka and Reeves had said their intention was to better represent WKU's international student population.

In the recordHerald, 10 Sep 2013

11 September 2013

SGA reviewed 24-hour dining, grading and registration proposals

SGA gave first read to a proposal for a 24-hour on-campus dining option, with the Organizational Aid Committee sponsoring the resolution and assistant vice president for auxiliary services Gary Meszaros set to attend the next meeting. Reeves told senators Provost Gordon Emslie was reviving a plus/minus grading proposal and had brought priority registration and major-declaration changes to University Senate.

In the recordHerald, 11 Sep 2013

12 September 2013

Senate passed international student seat amendment

President Keyana Boka and executive vice president Mark Reeves authored a constitutional amendment adding a senate seat for Navitas or English as a Second Language international students. The Judicial Council had ruled an earlier version unconstitutional, but after a revision in an emergency meeting the Senate passed it with only two votes against. Boka said it would make WKU's SGA the first student government in the state with an international senate seat.

In the recordHerald, 12 Sep 2013

12 September 2013

Student petition for 24-hour dining collects 700 signatures for SGA

Bowling Green sophomore Nick Conrad, a McCormack Hall resident assistant, gathered more than 700 signatures in about a week on a petition asking for a 24-hour dining option on campus, with a stated goal of 5,000. Conrad said he studied late and knew many students on similar schedules. He had met with SGA representatives who were interested in the petition.

In the recordHerald, 12 Sep 2013

19 September 2013

Fall election drew 564 voters, created international seat

A total of 564 voters cast ballots in the fall SGA election. A referendum creating the Navitas/ESL international student senate seat passed with 310 of 426 votes, or 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, with Jay Todd Richey taking 27 percent of the vote, and most college senate seats went to unopposed candidates.

In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2013

19 September 2013

564 vote in fall election; referendum creates the Navitas/ESL seat

A total of 564 students voted in the fall election. The referendum creating a Navitas and English as a Second Language international student senate seat drew 426 votes and passed with 310 yes votes, 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, led by Jay Todd Richey with 27 percent, along with two graduate senators, a Gatton Academy senator and an Arts and Letters senator.

In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2013

26 September 2013

Senate funds transcript vouchers with $300

SGA passed a bill allotting $300 to the Transcript Voucher Program fund, letting students collect vouchers from the SGA office instead of paying the $7 transcript fee. Academic Affairs committee head Megan Skaggs, who wrote the bill, said students already paid a great deal in tuition and fees. Funding for the long-running program had to be renewed by senate vote each time more money was needed.

In the recordHerald, 26 Sep 2013

9 October 2013

Resolution targets the internet policy behind WKU's FIRE red light rating

A resolution by Director of Public Relations Laura Harper received its first read, supporting amendment of university internet usage policies that the Foundation for Individual Rights in Education had deemed a violation of free speech. FIRE had given WKU a red light rating because at least one handbook policy violated the First Amendment. Computing Policy 12-13, covering email content likely to be perceived as offensive or disparaging, was the specific cause.

In the recordHerald, 9 Oct 2013

10 October 2013

SGA finalized $125,000 budget

SGA finalized a $125,000 budget for the 2013-14 year, funded from student tuition at about $6.25 per student, after a planned funding increase did not come through. The organizational aid committee was allotted $30,000, with campus organizations able to receive up to $500 each. The executive discretionary fund held $5,900, part of which covered a Washington, D.C. higher education lobbying trip by Boka and Reeves.

In the recordHerald, 10 Oct 2013

10 October 2013

SGA finalizes a $125,000 budget with no planned increase

SGA finalized a 2013-14 budget of $125,000 drawn from student tuition, after not receiving a planned increase. Director of Public Relations Laura Harper said the figure equated to $6.25 per student. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay, who built the budget, said senate discretionary spending required a senate majority and executive discretionary spending required an executive committee majority.

In the recordHerald, 10 Oct 2013

15 October 2013Other

Safe Ride ran a booth at Homecoming tailgating

SGA members staffed a Safe Ride promotional booth during tailgating for the home football game on 15 October 2013 and gave a presentation at halftime. Attendance at that evening's senate meeting was lighter than usual as a result, and the meeting was cut short, though a resolution on internet usage policy and a bill funding identification vouchers both passed.

In the recordHerald, 17 Oct 2013 - "SGA passes bills for ID vouchers funding"

17 October 2013

Internet policy resolution and ID voucher bill pass at a short meeting

With attendance thinned by a home football game where SGA ran a Safe Ride promotional booth, the senate passed Resolution 3-13-F on internet usage policies and Bill 2-13-F funding identification vouchers. Two further bills went into first read, one on organizational aid and one funding six winter term scholarship sessions. Laura Harper introduced the internet policy resolution.

In the recordHerald, 17 Oct 2013

24 October 2013

SGA spends $1,598 on five charging stations with the libraries

SGA and WKU Libraries agreed to buy five KwikBoost phone and laptop charging stations for $1,598, each with eight charging attachments. President Keyana Boka said Dean of University Libraries Connie Foster brought her the idea. Three stations were planned for the Educational Resources Center, Helm 100 and Helm 2, with the other two going to the Glasgow and Owensboro campuses.

In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2013

31 October 2013

Priority registration complaints spurred open forum

Student complaints over new two-tier priority registration rules, including a 16-credit-hour cap during the priority period, pushed SGA to schedule a Nov. 12 open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie. Honors College seniors told senator Tyler Scaff some were considering dropping the honors major over the change. Boka said she had no official stance yet, though SGA had earlier approved the change through Reeves's vote at University Senate.

In the recordHerald, 31 Oct 2013

5 November 2013

Herald editorial faulted SGA over registration policy

A Herald editorial accused SGA of failing to represent students on the new priority-registration hour cap, saying executive vice president Mark Reeves voted for the policy at University Senate on Sept. 10 without SGA questioning or debating it first. The editorial argued SGA had one job, representing students, and had not done it on this issue.

In the recordHerald, 5 Nov 2013

5 November 2013

Herald editorial says SGA failed students on priority registration

A Herald editorial criticized SGA for scheduling an open forum on the new priority registration policy for Nov. 12, after the policy was already set to govern fall registration. The policy limited students with priority registration to 16 hours on their priority day, excluding seniors and graduate students. The editorial said SGA had missed the chance to represent students on an exclusively student issue, pointing to failures at a Sept. 10 meeting.

In the recordHerald, 5 Nov 2013

7 November 2013

Thompson Complex North Wing set to close permanently

Boka announced at the Tuesday SGA meeting that Thompson Complex North Wing, home to the biology and chemistry departments, would close permanently the next semester because the building could not be maintained over the winter. The building had been labeled for demolition since 2005, and its demolition along with renovation of the Center Wing was the university's top capital priority before the Kentucky General Assembly.

In the recordHerald, 7 Nov 2013

13 November 2013

Provost and registrar face students at SGA's priority registration forum

SGA hosted an open forum on priority registration during its weekly meeting, with Provost Gordon Emslie and University Registrar Freida Eggleton answering questions. The policy, already in effect for spring registration, split priority registration into a need tier and a benefit tier and capped qualifying students at 16 credit hours until open registration. Seniors and graduate students still registered first and were not subject to the cap.

In the recordHerald, 13 Nov 2013

20 November 2013

South Campus forum turns on the closing of the campus store

SGA held its weekly meeting at South Campus as an open forum and President Keyana Boka asked those present to discuss the recent closing of the South Campus WKU store. Senators debated the lack of communication between the officials who closed the store and South Campus students. Executive Vice President Mark Reeves said the same thing had happened the previous year when the food court closed, calling it part of a broader failure to consult South Campus students.

In the recordHerald, 20 Nov 2013

3 December 2013

Judicial Council voided Talisman fee stance reversal

After the yearbook's budget was cut to $127,000, senator Chris Costa moved at the Nov. 19 meeting to revoke SGA's stance supporting a $9 student fee for the Talisman that students had approved on a 2005 ballot, and two-thirds of SGA voted to reverse the stance. The Judicial Council ruled Costa's motion unconstitutional on Nov. 21, and also ruled the original 2005 policy unconstitutional because it was never passed according to SGA policy. Talisman editors then met with Boka and SGA members to discuss long-term funding options.

In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2013

3 December 2013

Talisman brings its funding shortfall to SGA

Talisman representatives met President Keyana Boka and Brad Cockrel on Nov. 29 to discuss long-term options for paying for the yearbook. The previous May the Talisman had faced a proposed $93,000 cut, 47 percent of its $198,000 budget, before an alumni-backed "Save the Talisman" campaign reduced the cut. Its budget stood at $127,000, including $45,000 in one-time university funds.

In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2013

3 December 2013

Student on crutches brings a bus stop bench proposal to the senate

Covington senior Logan Eckler went before SGA on Nov. 19 to propose benches at campus bus stops after several days on crutches following a judo injury. He said the bus system was invaluable for students who had difficulty walking but that few stops had seats. Eckler said the same problem affected pregnant students and people with disabilities, and that SGA senators he knew had recommended he bring it forward.

In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2013

6 February 2014

SGA reconvened, planned Frankfort rally against budget cuts

At the first spring meeting, Boka announced a planned trip to Frankfort called "Rally for Retention" in response to WKU's $1.8 million state budget cut, with speeches and one-on-one meetings with legislators. Reeves warned that tough budget cuts were coming, and the body reviewed a proposal to revise the change-of-major advising process. Five members had resigned the previous semester, leaving the legislative research and public relations chairs among the vacant seats.

In the recordHerald, 6 Feb 2014

6 February 2014

SGA plans a Frankfort rally over WKU's $1.8 million budget cut

At the first spring meeting President Keyana Boka announced SGA would organize a trip to Frankfort called "Rally for Retention" in response to WKU's $1.8 million budget cut, with speeches and one-on-one meetings with legislators. Executive Vice President Mark Reeves outlined the two-year state budget then being voted on and said students needed to be involved. Boka also reported talks with dining services about 24-hour dining, with Einstein's Bagels under consideration for its location in a 24-hour study area.

In the recordHerald, 6 Feb 2014

13 February 2014

Executive Council nullified judicial appointment amendment

An amendment stripping the SGA president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and raising the number of justices to seven passed at the Tuesday meeting, over Boka's objection that it bypassed presidential appointment and the senate. After the meeting the Executive Council reviewed the constitution and determined too few senators had attended for the vote to count, sending the amendment back to first read. The SGA office also temporarily moved to Garrett after flooding in Cravens.

In the recordHerald, 13 Feb 2014

13 February 2014

Executive council voids an amendment stripping the president's judicial appointments

After review, SGA declared unconstitutional an amendment that had passed at its Tuesday meeting removing the president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and expanding the council to seven justices. President Keyana Boka said the president is elected by the student body to make appointments in all three branches and said she was wary of the direction. Chief Justice Seth Church argued that vesting appointments in the executive branch as a whole created a fairer system.

In the recordHerald, 13 Feb 2014

26 February 2014

Mid-year budget report showed $46,883 surplus

SGA's mid-year budget report showed a $46,883.62 surplus on its $125,000 budget. The Senate approved Bill 3-14-S allocating organizational funds and suspended its bylaws to pass Resolution 3-14-S supporting WKU's participation in the Campus Pride Index, and approved Hannah Neeper, Elizabeth Gribbins and AJ Stewart as new senators as six senate seats remained open.

In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2014

26 February 2014

Budget report shows a $46,883.62 surplus

SGA released its 2013-14 budget showing $125,000 budgeted and a surplus of $46,883.62. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay said the budget had changed little since December and that she had more funds to allocate back to the student body. SGA allocated $54,000 to the legislative branch for items such as organizational aid and grants, and approved three new senators at the same meeting.

In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2014

18 March 2014

SGA unanimously backs taking the Campus Pride Index

An SGA proposal that WKU take the Campus Pride Index, a survey measuring campus friendliness toward LGBT students, passed unanimously and was submitted to the Administrative Council. Student Identity Outreach president Andrew Salman first proposed it to the Office of Diversity, and senator Nicki Seay carried it into SGA. Salman said the index would diagnose areas where the university was not meeting the needs of its queer students, and Seay said WKU had never taken it before.

In the recordHerald, 18 Mar 2014

15 April 2014

Turnout falls to 908, down 555 votes from the previous year

A Herald editorial reported that SGA voter turnout for the spring election was 908, down 555 votes from the year before. The editorial called turnout below 1,000 pathetic and said the student body could and should do better. It noted that the SGA president represents students at the Board of Regents and that SGA funds organizational aid and extended library hours.

In the recordHerald, 15 Apr 2014

21 April 2014Festival

SGA opened Earth Week by planting the community garden

SGA and the Office of Sustainability kicked off Earth Week on 21 April 2014 with a planting party in the community garden behind the sustainability house at 503 Regents Avenue. President Keyana Boka said she was glad SGA could support the garden, which SGA's campus improvement committee then took on maintaining, growing tomatoes, squash, sunflowers and peppers. Garden coordinator Beth McGrew said the aim was to build community through sustainability and strengthen students' connection to their food.

In the recordHerald, 21 Apr 2014 - "SGA and Office of Sustainability Kick-Off Earth Week"

24 April 2014Service

Campus-wide safety walk from Centennial Mall

SGA held a campus safety walk starting at Centennial Mall at 6:30 p.m. on 24 April 2014, inviting students to point out anywhere they felt unsafe, whether dark or unstable. President Keyana Boka said the purpose was to promote safety.

In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2014 - "SGA hosts campus wide safety walk"

May 2014

Final meeting passed Good Samaritan resolution, funding bills

At the last meeting of the semester, Boka announced students would face a 4.8 percent tuition increase, about $209 more per semester for most, alongside a $4.2 million increase in student financial assistance. The Senate suspended its bylaws to pass a slate of bills funding Summer Term assistance, student organizations, student research and an Earth Week planting party. Resolution 6-14-S passed in support of adopting a Good Samaritan Policy protecting students who call 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses.

In the recordHerald, 1 May 2014

May 2014

SGA suspends its bylaws to clear bills at the last meeting

At the final meeting of the semester SGA suspended its bylaws to pass multiple bills on first read, beginning with Bill 17-14-S allocating $1,817.10. President Keyana Boka reported a 4.8 percent tuition increase that would cost most students about $209 more per semester, along with a $4.2 million increase for student financial assistance and a one percent faculty salary adjustment. Speaker Paige Settles said one remaining scholarship bill would be handled at a short meeting during the end-of-year banquet.

Keyana Boka - Student Government Association UA12/2/1 2014 Graduation Special Section

2014-15

Nicki Taylor (president)

31 entries · 34 index lines

28 August 2014

SGA opened the year with a $21,000 scholarship program

SGA began the year under new president Nicki Seay, a Crofton senior, working alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles. The association expanded its summer and winter term need-based scholarship program from the previous year's $6,000 to $21,000, funded in part by an anonymous donation. Seay named student involvement, retention and graduation her first priorities.

In the recordHerald, 28 Aug 2014

2 September 2014campus

Downing Student Union celebrated its community opening

WKU held a ceremonial community opening for Downing Student Union after a two-year, $49 million renovation; the building had opened to students the week before. Students paid $36 million of the cost through a $70-per-semester fee, and the renovation began as an SGA initiative in 2011. SGA President Nicki Seay attended alongside President Gary Ransdell and other officials.

In the recordHerald, 2 Sep 2014

25 September 2014

Fall election drew 742 voters and seated 17 senators

SGA announced its fall election results around 12:20 a.m. in the Senate Chamber of Downing Student Union. There were 742 voters and 17 senators were elected, including three freshman senators led by Emily Pride with 281 votes. President Nicki Seay called the election very competitive, noting not everyone who ran won a seat.

In the recordHerald, 25 Sep 2014

25 September 2014

742 vote in fall election as 17 senators are elected

SGA announced fall election results around 12:20 a.m. before a crowd of about 15 people in the DSU Senate Chamber, with 742 voters and 17 senators elected. President Nicki Seay said the election was competitive and not everyone who ran won a seat. Emily Pride led the freshman senators with 281 votes, and the senators-elect were sworn in at the Sept. 30 meeting.

In the recordHerald, 25 Sep 2014

October 2014

Commuter focus group brings parking fixes to the senate

Campus Improvements Committee Chair Tyler Scaff reported that a commuter focus group had proposed solutions to campus parking problems, including adding a function to the iWKU app that would list each lot with the number of spaces available. A South Campus park and ride was also proposed. Scaff said the committee was working on other projects including an SGA garden plot at the Office of Sustainability.

In the recordHerald, 1 Oct 2014

15 October 2014

Senate defeated a nonsectarian prayer policy resolution

After more than 20 minutes of debate, the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was split three ways among nonsectarian prayer, sectarian prayer and no prayer at all. The same night, senators passed Bill 9-14-F allocating $250 in organizational aid to the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity.

In the recordHerald, 15 Oct 2014

15 October 2014

Senate defeats the nonsectarian prayer policy resolution

After more than 20 minutes of debate the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. Chief of Staff Seth Church explained that a nonsectarian prayer differs from a sectarian one that refers to a specific deity. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was divided, which caused the resolution to be voted down.

In the recordHerald, 15 Oct 2014

22 October 2014

SGA funds an emergency food program for students with frozen accounts

Bill 10-14-F passed without debate, allocating $500 from legislative discretionary funds toward the $3,600 Emergency Food Pilot Program. The program gave the first 50 students who could show their university account was locked 10 free meals through Fresh Food Company waivers. Author William Berry said it would let those students eat for a few days while they worked on paying their bills.

In the recordHerald, 22 Oct 2014

29 October 2014

Glasgow rewrites its constitution after struggling to keep members

Amendments to Glasgow's SGA constitution received their first read on the main campus. Chief of Staff Seth Church said Glasgow's constitution had been modeled on the main campus document and that the regional campus had struggled with student involvement and retaining SGA members, so it was decided to change the constitution drastically. Glasgow's SGA had already voted to approve the amendments, leaving the main campus senate to ratify them.

In the recordHerald, 29 Oct 2014

30 October 2014

President establishes a Cultural and Diversity Affairs Committee

SGA created a Cultural and Diversity Affairs Committee chaired by Seth Church, who developed the idea for a leadership practicum focused on diversity within SGA and on campus. Church said he collaborated with President Nicki Taylor to create it. Taylor said making SGA more diverse had been an ongoing conversation since her first year and that establishing ad hoc committees was a power she held as president.

In the recordHerald, 30 Oct 2014

20 November 2014

Executive Cabinet vetoed the smoke-free campus resolution

The senate passed Resolution 11-14-F, supporting a smoke-free campus, on a 14-10 vote, but the SGA Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Chief of Staff Seth Church argued it was unfair to ban smoking for students required to live on campus for two years. Senators retained the power to override the veto with a two-thirds vote.

In the recordHerald, 20 Nov 2014

20 November 2014

Executive Cabinet vetoes the smoke-free campus resolution hours after it passes

Resolution 11-14-F supporting a smoke-free campus passed the senate 14-10, and the Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Author William Berry said he left the location of any smoking areas to the administration and that the ban infringed no student's rights, while senator Haley Jones countered that smoking is legal and students over 18 can buy tobacco. The policy would not have limited other tobacco products or electronic cigarettes.

In the recordHerald, 20 Nov 2014

4 December 2014

Veto override failed; alcohol policy resolution passed

At the final meeting of the fall semester, the senate failed to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free resolution, and President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official veto statement citing enforcement, housing requirements and practicality. The senate then passed Resolution 13-14-F, supporting amendments to WKU's alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct to let students 21 and older purchase and possess alcohol on campus. Co-author Jody Dahmer called the existing policy ineffective and hard to enforce fairly.

In the recordHerald, 4 Dec 2014

4 December 2014

Senate fails to override the smoking veto and passes an alcohol resolution

A motion to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free resolution failed at the final meeting of the semester, which ran two and a half hours. President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official statement, which cited enforcement, housing requirements and practicality as the reasons for the veto. The senate passed a resolution supporting changes to WKU's alcohol policy the same night.

In the recordHerald, 4 Dec 2014

14 December 2014

President Taylor addressed December graduates

SGA President Nicki Taylor spoke at WKU's December commencement, telling graduates to celebrate what they had accomplished: "You have the rest of your life to look forward to." She had opened the year in August under her previous surname, Seay, and was going by Taylor in Herald coverage by mid-October.

In the recordHerald, 14 Dec 2014

3 February 2015

Limited smoking campus resolution passed 13-11

SGA passed Resolution 1-15-S, supporting a limited smoking campus, by a 13-11 vote. The resolution would restrict tobacco use to 39 designated areas that the Administrative Council would gradually phase out over three years, while leaving electronic cigarettes and smokeless tobacco unrestricted. Co-author Seth Church said it was roughly the fifth version of the resolution since the smoking debate began the previous semester.

In the recordHerald, 3 Feb 2015

3 February 2015

SGA backs limiting smoking to 39 areas and phasing them out

The senate voted on Resolution 1-15-S supporting a limited smoking campus, restricting tobacco use to 39 designated areas. The resolution called for the Administrative Council to create a plan reducing those areas and gradually phasing them out over three years, and would not have limited electronic cigarettes or smokeless tobacco. The existing policy allowed smoking anywhere on campus at least 30 feet from buildings.

In the recordHerald, 3 Feb 2015

4 February 2015

President Taylor abstained on smoking vote as a sitting regent

The Bowling Green Daily News reported that Nicki Taylor, in addition to serving as SGA president, sat on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking-campus proposal because of that seat.

In the recordBowling Green Daily News, 4 Feb 2015

10 February 2015

SGA pursues new student fees; Ransdell calls even $4 difficult

SGA said it would pursue further fee resolutions after passing one the previous semester supporting a $4 per year fee for the Student Legal Services Clinic, and had begun asking students about a roughly $30 fee to fund an estimated $10 million parking structure. President Nicki Taylor said the ideas grew out of student interest in conversation with President Gary Ransdell. Ransdell said approving even a $4 fee would be difficult and that he would be reluctant to take it to the Board of Regents.

In the recordHerald, 10 Feb 2015

3 March 2015

SGA backed a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 fee

SGA passed a resolution supporting construction of a new parking structure on part of Creason Lot, funded by a $30-per-semester tuition increase. Authors Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry estimated the roughly 500-car garage would take about 18 months to build. Chief of Staff Seth Church objected that the plan was rushed and left out regional campuses.

In the recordHerald, 3 Mar 2015

3 March 2015

SGA endorses a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 tuition rise

SGA passed a resolution supporting a new parking structure funded by a $30 increase in tuition each semester. The resolution placed the garage on part of Creason Lot and suggested a temporary gravel lot on the site of Tate Page Hall after its anticipated demolition. President Nicki Taylor said the structure had been before the parking and transportation committee for the whole academic year, and the authors were Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry.

In the recordHerald, 3 Mar 2015

4 March 2015

Ransdell formally responded to four SGA resolutions

President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff his official response to four SGA resolutions on limited smoking, campus alcohol sales, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. He announced a six-person ad hoc committee to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017 and a restaurant in the Garrett Conference Center that could serve beer in the evenings. He said the parking and legal services fees would need Board of Regents and Council on Postsecondary Education approval.

In the recordHerald, 4 Mar 2015

4 March 2015

Ransdell answers four SGA resolutions by email to faculty and staff

President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff with his official response to four SGA resolutions covering limited smoking, amending the alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct for students over 21, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. On smoking he said he would form a six-person ad hoc committee of students, faculty and staff to recommend how to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017. On alcohol he said a restaurant facility in the Garrett Conference Center would be built where beer and possibly wine could be served.

18 March 2015

Breast milk expression resolution passes unanimously without debate

Resolution 4-15-S, supporting creation and maintenance of private areas on campus where students, faculty and staff could express breast milk, passed unanimously and without debate. Chief of Staff Seth Church, who wrote it, said a non-traditional student who had just had her third child brought the problem to him and found the existing unlocked room in a department hall uncomfortable. Church said he wanted no fewer than three permanent spaces.

2 April 2015

Jay Todd Richey won the SGA presidency, 874 votes to 524

Jay Todd Richey defeated senator Brian Chism for SGA president, 63 percent to 37 percent, or 874 votes to 524, with results announced about 20 minutes after TopNet polls closed at 11:59 p.m. Wednesday. Nolan Miles ran unopposed for a second term as executive vice president, and Liz Koehler won the administrative vice president race with 66 percent over J. William Berry. Twenty of 34 senatorial candidates won seats.

2 April 2015

Campaign spending caps range from $350 for president to $50 for senators

Under the spring 2014 election packet, SGA presidential candidates could not spend more than $350, executive vice president candidates $300, administrative vice president candidates $250 and senatorial candidates $50. President Nicki Taylor said she ran unopposed and did not spend a cent, but pointed to the contested 2013 race between Cain Alvey and Keyana Boka. Taylor said Alvey spent every dollar of his $350 limit.

An election result challenged and upheld

Anonymous accusations alleged Jay Todd Richey had breached election codes on poster placement. The judicial council warned him against future violations and confirmed he had rightfully won.

Two hours of debate over an African Student Union reimbursement

Bill 8-15-S, allocating $500 to the WKU African Student Union as reimbursement for attending a conference at the University of Kentucky, passed 12 to four with many senators abstaining, after a meeting that ran two hours and ended with fewer senators present. Acting president Henry Nottinson said the reimbursement would lessen the burden on members who had paid out of pocket. He said the group did not have enough money to keep going.

2015-16

Jay Todd Richey (president)

28 entries · 47 index lines

27 August 2015

Richey outlined fall goals, MyCampusToo launch

Opening his first term, President Jay Todd Richey said he wanted more executive-cabinet and senate communication and more outreach to international students and regional campuses, and confirmed his campaign initiative MyCampusToo would launch that semester. Executive Vice President Nolan Miles said he would push senators to sit on university committees and revive the Dine with Decision Makers event.

In the recordHerald, 27 Aug 2015

10 September 2015

SGA tables Confucius Institute resolution, creates sustainability committee

The senate tabled Resolution 1-15-F, which would have concurred with the University Senate in asking President Gary Ransdell to revisit WKU's contract with Hanban, citing uncertainty about the contract terms. At the same meeting Bill 1-15-F recognizing an Elizabethtown/Fort Knox student body association and Bill 2-15-F supporting the MyCampusToo initiative both passed unanimously, as did an executive proposal creating a sustainability committee. President Jay Todd Richey said of the Hanban contract that it was "definitely one sided."

In the recordHerald, 10 Sep 2015

15 September 2015

SGA budget fell by $19,500

SGA's budget dropped $19,500 from the previous year, largely because a $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut another $4,500 in reallocations. Organizational funding took the hardest hit, losing $9,000, and scholarship pools for Academic Affairs and Student Affairs each fell by more than $5,000. Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reallocated $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships to soften the loss.

In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2015

15 September 2015

SGA budget falls by $19,500

SGA's budget dropped $19,500 from the prior year after a $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut a further $4,500. Organizational funding took the largest hit, losing $9,000, and Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler moved $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships. The Herald noted WKU's SGA budget stood at $138,500 against the University of Louisville's $1.2 million.

In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2015

15 September 2015Lecture

SGA paid half the fare for a Latino leadership keynote

On 15 September 2015 the senate unanimously passed Bill 4-15-F, allocating $200 from legislative discretionary funds for the seminar "Si, Se Puede: Leadership in the Latino Community." The money covered half the estimated travel costs of keynote speaker Johana Lopez, a WKU alumna and Houston-based leadership coach, with the Hilltopper Organization of Latin American Students covering the rest. The same meeting passed $1,200 for study away scholarships.

$200 toward the keynote speaker's travel; $1,200 in study away scholarships

In the recordHerald, 17 Sep 2015 - "SGA allocates funds to study away scholarships"

22 September 2015

Senate voted to disapprove Confucius Institute approval process

The Student Senate voted overwhelmingly to pass a resolution disapproving of how the Confucius Institute building project was approved, after President Gary Ransdell signed the contract in China in December 2014 and the Board of Regents, including the Student Regent, voted on it more than a month later without full details disclosed. Richey said the vote was not meant to set a precedent beyond ensuring the Board had full information before acting.

In the recordHerald, 24 Sep 2015

24 September 2015

Senate votes 21-4 to disapprove Confucius Institute building process

The senate passed Resolution 2-15-F disapproving of what it called the nontransparent procedure by which the Model Confucius Institute building was authorized. Several senators argued the institute was an asset to WKU and Bowling Green, while Campus Improvement Chairman Zachary Jones backed the resolution as an expression of student opinion. Richey wrote separately that some senators had warned the vote would make "powerful enemies" for SGA.

In the recordHerald, 24 Sep 2015

30 September 2015

Regents decline to revisit Confucius contract, closing SGA debate

Richey told the senate the Board of Regents had decided at its Sept. 25 meeting not to revisit the contract for the Confucius Institute building, and said he wished to close SGA's debate on the matter. "Just to clarify, it's a done deal, the building will be built," he said. In the same report he told senators state appropriations had fallen from 47 percent of WKU's operating budget in 1998 to 18 percent for 2015-16.

In the recordHerald, 30 Sep 2015

13 October 2015Tradition

Planning began for SGA's fiftieth anniversary

President Jay Todd Richey told the Herald in October 2015 that SGA's fiftieth anniversary would fall in 2016 and that a gala was among the ideas being discussed, along with inviting alumni and former members back to see what had changed. No date had been fixed and Richey said the plans were still in the idea phase and would be opened to all members and interested students. SGA had last marked itself in 2006, for the fortieth.

In the recordHerald, 13 Oct 2015 - "SGA plans to celebrate 50th anniversary"

12 November 2015

SGA cabinet pulls 'Spirit Masters' from pub-naming ballot

The executive cabinet removed the name "Spirit Masters" from the Dub the Pub ballot after administrators said it demeaned WKU's student ambassador group, though the name was in second place at the time. Topper Tavern won with 480 of 2,132 votes cast. Senator Chase Coffey said Richey closed the issue without letting senators speak and objected that "Topped Off" had been left on the ballot.

In the recordHerald, 12 Nov 2015

18 November 2015

Senate backed meningitis vaccine requirement, amended bylaws

The Senate unanimously passed Resolution 6-15-F supporting a meningococcal meningitis vaccination requirement for incoming freshmen in on-campus housing beginning with the class of 2020, and unanimously passed Bill 10-15-F amending SGA's bylaws. Richey reported that his fall listening tours of the regional campuses had gone well and turned up how different those campuses were from main campus.

In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2015

19 November 2015

Senate backs meningitis vaccine requirement for on-campus freshmen

Resolution 6-15-F, supporting a meningococcal meningitis vaccination requirement for incoming freshmen living in on-campus housing beginning with the class of 2020, passed unanimously. Bill 10-15-F amending the SGA bylaws also passed unanimously. Richey reported back from listening tours at the Glasgow, Owensboro and Elizabethtown/Fort Knox campuses, saying a full-time security officer was Glasgow's top priority.

In the recordHerald, 19 Nov 2015

3 December 2015

Chief Justice resigned after censure hearing backlash

The Judicial Council unanimously declined to censure senator John Winstead, whom it had investigated over an "impeach Ransdell" sign and a mocking Facebook post about President Ransdell, ruling his actions were protected free speech. Winstead called the fact he was investigated at all "the problem I'm objecting to." Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell then announced she would step down at the end of the semester, saying the council had been publicly ridiculed and lacked support from fellow SGA members.

In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2015

3 December 2015

Judicial Council strips funding from physics and art departments

The Judicial Council ruled Bills 8-15-F and 9-15-F unconstitutional under Bylaw 6.1, which stated SGA may allocate funds solely to students, voiding $1,500 for the physics department and up to $759 for the art department. Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell said money given to departments benefits faculty and staff as well as students. The council encouraged the student League of Sculptors to apply instead for $500 in organizational aid.

In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2015

3 December 2015

Judicial Council declines to censure senator over 'impeach Ransdell' sign; chief justice resigns

The Judicial Council voted unanimously not to censure Senator John Winstead, who had been investigated over a sign at the homecoming game and a Facebook image mocking President Gary Ransdell, finding his conduct protected by the First Amendment. Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell resigned effective the end of the semester. Winstead said the process was "fundamentally flawed" and objected to being investigated at all.

In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2015

26 January 2016

SGA refuses to enforce the campus smoking phaseout

After hearing from a University of Kentucky representative who explained UK pays ambassadors to enforce its tobacco ban and requires them to report violators, SGA declined to assemble the enforcement corps Ransdell's email had described. "SGA has no intention on actually being the group that enforces this," Richey said, adding that he personally disagreed with the ban but would adhere to it. The policy proceeded as voluntary compliance backed by signage.

In the recordHerald, 26 Jan 2016

28 January 2016

Administration overrode student vote on pub name

Richey announced that administrators had renamed the future Garrett Conference Center pub "Topper Grill and Pub," setting aside the name students chose in SGA's "Dub the Pub" contest, Topper Tavern. Richey said Ransdell wanted to downplay the alcohol theme and called himself "very disappointed," saying the move made SGA question how much the administration listened to students. At the same meeting SGA introduced the RAVE Guardian campus safety app.

In the recordHerald, 28 Jan 2016

28 January 2016

Administration overrides student vote on pub name

Richey announced that administrators had changed the winning pub name from Topper Tavern and Grill to Topper Grill and Pub, a decision he said was made by former Student Affairs Vice President Howard Bailey and reflected Ransdell's wish to downplay the alcohol theme. "I was very disappointed," Richey said, adding that it made SGA question how much the administration listens to students. The same meeting introduced the RAVE Guardian campus safety app.

In the recordHerald, 28 Jan 2016

2 February 2016

Ransdell announced retirement amid state budget cuts

President Gary Ransdell announced he would step down as WKU's ninth president on June 30, 2017, triggering a presidential search. The announcement came the same week new Gov. Matt Bevin ordered an immediate 4.5 percent cut to WKU's state funding and proposed a 9 percent cut, with future funding shifted to a performance-based pool. The changes framed much of SGA's advocacy for the rest of the year.

In the recordHerald, 2 Feb 2016

17 February 2016

Senate opposed state tuition-freeze bill

The senate approved Resolution 2-16-S opposing Kentucky Senate Bill 75, which would have frozen resident tuition at 2015-16 levels for four years. Richey argued such freezes were "dangerous risks" that could wreck universities and cost students more in the long run. At the same meeting, Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, about $1,301.

In the recordHerald, 17 Feb 2016

17 February 2016

SGA opposes state tuition-freeze bill; Richey says he appointed 42 percent of the senate

Resolution 2-16-S, opposing Kentucky Senate Bill 75's four-year tuition freeze, passed after debate, with Richey arguing such measures "can end up wrecking universities and charging students even more in the long run." Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, a loss of $1,301.27. Richey also told senators appointments should be more democratic, noting he had appointed 42 percent of the sitting senate.

In the recordHerald, 17 Feb 2016

24 February 2016

Senators lobbied legislators in Frankfort

SGA members traveled to Frankfort to lobby against state budget cuts that could slash WKU funding by as much as 9 percent, meeting with eight state officials. Senators pressed for smaller cuts and restoration of need-based aid, citing figures that about 15,000 students were denied need-based financial aid the prior year. Both chambers of the General Assembly recognized SGA for its participation.

In the recordHerald, 24 Feb 2016

2 March 2016

Ransdell declined SGA's meningitis vaccine mandate

Richey read aloud a letter from Ransdell responding to Resolution 6-15-F, passed the previous semester, which supported requiring meningitis vaccinations for incoming freshmen living on campus starting with the class of 2020. Ransdell wrote that the university would highly recommend vaccination but "stop short of requiring it," citing a $143.77 cost for uninsured students at the Graves-Gilbert Clinic.

In the recordHerald, 2 Mar 2016

23 March 2016

Senate refuses to vote on Judicial Council's new election codes

The senate declined to vote on election codes drafted by the Judicial Council that would have cut senate campaign spending from $50 to $25 and limited candidates to three pieces of campaign material per building, placed only on bulletin boards. Richey, absent from the meeting, called the changes "too much red tape" and over-regulation. Chief Justice Amber Daniel scheduled a separate meeting for senators to propose changes.

In the recordHerald, 23 Mar 2016

6 April 2016

Senate passed guidelines for WKU's tenth president

The senate approved a resolution by John Winstead and Richey outlining what students wanted in WKU's tenth president, which Richey planned to use in his role on the presidential search committee. After debate, senators amended the sustainability clause to target improving WKU's AASHE STARS rating and voted to remove language about Jonesville "reparations" entirely, after disputing whether reparations or restitution was the right term.

In the recordHerald, 6 Apr 2016

6 April 2016

Senate strips reparations language from presidential-qualities resolution

Resolution 2-16-S, outlining recommended qualities for WKU's tenth president, passed after amendment. A clause on the displaced Jonesville community originally asking the next president to "offer solutions for how reparations can be made" was debated, changed to "restitution," then removed entirely by majority vote. A sustainability clause seeking a zero-emissions campus was also softened to a goal of raising WKU's AASHE STARS rating.

In the recordHerald, 6 Apr 2016

20 April 2016

Richey reelected in one of highest-turnout elections

Students reelected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president with 64 percent of the vote over Braxton Powell, in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history with 2,442 voters. Kate Hart, an Academic Affairs chairwoman and Richey's running mate, won executive vice president. Richey called the win "verification of promises kept."

In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2016

27 April 2016

Final meeting passes eSports, recycling and vegetarian dining resolutions

At its last meeting of the year the senate passed Resolution 3-16-S supporting recycling in the Downing Student Union, Garrett and Tower food courts, Resolution 4-16-S supporting creation of an eSports program and dedicated space, and Resolution 5-16-S supporting vegetarian options on the DSU meal plan. Bill 15-16-S allocated $600 to keep Helm-Cravens Library open until 2 a.m. during finals week. Nathan Cherry was elected speaker of the senate for 2016-17.

20 April 2016

Richey re-elected SGA president in high-turnout election

WKU students re-elected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president and elected Kate Hart as executive vice president in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history, with 2,442 voters. Richey defeated opponent Braxton Powell with 64 percent of the overall vote. Powell was elected a junior senator and his running mate Zach Jones a senior senator.

In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2016

19 August 2016

Student regent publishes dissent from Medical Center partnership

Jay Todd Richey, serving as student regent, wrote an open letter to students explaining his vote against the Board of Regents' 6-4-1 approval of a partnership with the Medical Center to construct a building housing an athletics practice facility and the Department of Physical Therapy. He argued the deal would tie WKU to a single health care provider for up to 99 years and place the university inside a long-running competition among Bowling Green providers. He wrote that although bound to uphold the board's decision, he believed it was a bad deal for WKU.

In the recordHerald, 19 Aug 2016

31 August 2016

SGA raises its own student office workers to $10.10 an hour

Richey told the senate SGA office workers would be paid $10.10 an hour, saying the raise reflected the rising cost of tuition. "SGA is making a stand and saying that students deserve this wage," he said. Chief facilities officer Bryan Russell also briefed senators that Parking Structure 3 in the Creason lot would add more than 500 spaces, with construction running from September to August 2017.

In the recordHerald, 31 Aug 2016

7 September 2016

Senate funds first disability scholarships after student testimony

Bill 4-16-F, creating scholarships for students with disabilities, passed unanimously after sophomore Brendan Ward told senators his ADHD and dyslexia had cost him merit scholarships and that he was at WKU "only by loans and the government." The bill drew $500 each from the football tabling and food lines of the SGA budget. Two other students, Cheyenne Mitchell and Francisco Serrano, addressed the senate about racist vandalism and discrimination on campus.

In the recordHerald, 7 Sep 2016

12 September 2016campus

Ransdell condemns racist incidents after notes, vandalism

In the weeks before, racist notes had been left in a WKU assistant dean's office and a racial slur was scratched into a student's car following a parking dispute. President Gary Ransdell called the acts "cowardly" and "heinous," said they did not reflect the university's values, and called for campus dialogue on intolerance.

In the recordWKMS, 12 Sep 2016

13 September 2016

Senators raise campus racism at first fall meeting

At the third meeting of the 15th Senate, student speakers Jeb Veeck, Francisco Serrano and Spencer Wells addressed the recent racist incidents on campus. Veeck suggested a Q&A session on the issue and Serrano urged senators to help end racism on campus.

In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 13 Sep 2016Read it here

20 September 2016Programme

SGA co-sponsored the International Diplomats' Home Away From Home

Bill 7-16-F allocated $250 from senate discretionary funding to International Enrollment Management for the International Diplomats' charity event Home Away From Home, held on 29 September 2016 at the Honors College and International Center. The event was built so international students could meet American students and Bowling Green organisations, with all proceeds going to the International Center of Kentucky and a small prize for whoever donated most. The bill passed unanimously on 27 September.

$250

In the recordSGA Bill 7-16-F, Funding for the International Diplomats Event "Home Away From Home"

21 September 2016

Senate seat left vacant all summer by an uncorrected election error

Speaker Nathan Cherry told the senate that eleven at-large seats should have been filled the previous spring but only ten were, leaving SGA one senator short through the summer. "I failed to catch that," Cherry said. Lucas Knight was selected to fill the seat, and Richey said he was exploring a hybrid arrangement letting students question anonymous presidential candidates online during the closed search.

In the recordHerald, 21 Sep 2016

4 October 2016Programme

Earn-A-Computer gave away its first desktop

SGA presented the first computer under its Earn-A-Computer programme on 4 October 2016, an iMac awarded free to Nashville junior Bobby Scott after he completed 35 hours of community service. Scott worked with the Intercultural Engagement Center and with children at Warren Elementary School. A computer information technology major whose own machine had recently died, he told the senate he had badly needed it. SGA ran the programme with WKU Resource Conservation.

In the recordHerald, 10 Oct 2016 - "SGA awards first desktop in computer program"

12 October 2016

Two SGA members resign amid racism complaint; investigation nullified

After Chief Justice Cody Cox told the Oct. 11 senate meeting he had received a complaint that several SGA members made racist remarks, senator Braxton Powell and justice John McKinney resigned the next morning, citing scheduling conflicts and personal reasons respectively; neither confirmed, denied, nor acknowledged any link between the resignations and the complaint. The Judicial Council's planned investigation was dropped because the students in question had already left SGA, and the organization never released the identities of the accused or the nature of the alleged remarks. President Richey and MyCampusToo chair Helen Vickrey issued a statement the next day condemning the alleged acts.

In the recordHerald, 17 Oct 2016

12 October 2016

SGA creates SAVES committee on sexual assault and suicide prevention

The senate created the Standing Against Violence and Ending Self-harm special committee to work on sexual assault prevention, suicide prevention and expanded mental health resources with the Counseling and Testing Center. Senator Francisco Serrano was named chair and described his own recent experience of having water thrown at him and racial slurs shouted while walking outside Downing Student Union. Freshman Ryan Linton told the senate WKU's harassment policy did not explicitly protect gender identity.

In the recordHerald, 12 Oct 2016

26 October 2016

Senate rejected 2.0 GPA bill, backed housing diversity

SGA rejected a bill that would have let students vote to lower the organization's GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0, a change supporters said would make the body more representative; a Twitter poll found 61 percent of respondents opposed it. The senate also approved a resolution asking Housing and Residence Life to address the lack of diversity in on-campus housing under the university's 10-year housing plan.

In the recordHerald, 26 Oct 2016

26 October 2016

Senate rejects GPA change again, approves housing diversity resolution

A bill to let students vote on lowering SGA's GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0 was rejected, with Senator Kaycee Gibson saying representatives "are expected to be elitist" and Public Relations Chair Alex Sergent saying "we're the cream of the crop." An SGA Twitter poll had found 61 percent of respondents opposed the change. The senate did approve a resolution asking Housing and Residence Life to integrate honors and international students across Southwest and Northeast halls rather than segregating them.

In the recordHerald, 26 Oct 2016

31 October 2016

Kentucky student body presidents demand restoration of the 'Powerball Promise'

Richey, as chair of the Board of Student Body Presidents of Kentucky, co-signed a published letter with the student presidents of nine other Kentucky institutions calling on Gov. Matt Bevin and the legislature to stop diverting lottery money from need-based College Access Program and Kentucky Tuition Grant aid. The letter cited Kentucky Center for Economic Policy figures that underfunding had limited scholarships for 15,000 to 20,000 qualifying students in 2016. It named Bevin's veto of House Bill 10 as having blocked restoration of the funding.

In the recordHerald, 31 Oct 2016

SGA ran a Ride To Vote service on election day, 8 November 2016, driving any WKU student without transport to and from the polling stations. The programme was discussed at the senate meeting of 1 November alongside the Board of Student Body Presidents' letter to Governor Matt Bevin asking that lottery money be kept in need-based student financial aid.
