Bill 19-16-F allocated $1,200 from legislative discretionary funding to extend Helm-Cravens Library's hours during finals week in autumn 2016 and spring 2017, keeping it open until 2 a.m. Sunday through Thursday instead of midnight. The bill recorded that SGA had a standing tradition of paying for extended library hours each year, and that the library's signage would credit the sponsorship. It passed on 15 November 2016.

SGA launches SafeWalk and makes diversity and sustainability committees permanent

The senate approved bills making the Sustainability and MyCampusToo committees permanent standing committees under the constitution, and renamed MyCampusToo the Committee for Diversity and Inclusion after some found the old name "offensive and not inclusive." 30 November 2016

SGA created Jonesville scholarship fund

The senate created a scholarship memorializing Jonesville, the African American community founded by freed slaves in the 1870s that stood on land now occupied by Smith Stadium, Nick Denes Field and Downing Student Union until WKU bought and demolished it in the late 1960s. Senators debated whether the award should go only to African American students as repayment for Jonesville's condemnation or be opened to all minority students.

In the recordHerald, 30 Nov 2016

30 November 2016

Senate creates Jonesville Memorial Scholarship after debate over eligibility

SGA allocated $750, matched by $100 from the Center for Citizenship and Social Justice, for a scholarship memorializing Jonesville, the Black community WKU bought and displaced in the late 1960s for under $200,000. Senators debated opening it to all minority students, but the bill passed in its original form restricting it to first-year African American students from Warren County or Bowling Green schools. Senator Dillon McCormick called it "a kind of symbolic gesture to atone for the wrong that we did."

Safe Ride bus service cut on Thursdays as ridership collapses

SGA ended Thursday operation of its Safe Ride Purple Line after ridership fell to about one rider per hour, against twenty per hour on Saturdays. GPA requirement lowered to 2.0 by exactly the required margin

Judicial Council exemptions turn the presidential race into a three-way contest

19 April 2017

Andi Dahmer elected to succeed Richey

Louisville sophomore Andi Dahmer, a senator and chair of the MyCampusToo committee, was elected the next student body president, winning 930 of 1,579 votes cast against Kenan Mujkanovic's 305 and Lily Nellans's 212. Her running mates Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry won executive vice president and administrative vice president. Dahmer said she would start with legislation on study abroad affordability and sensitivity training to improve retention among marginalized groups.

19 April 2017campus

Dahmer elected; all six referendums pass

Andi Dahmer won the presidency with 930 of 1,579 votes cast, ahead of Kenan Mujkanovic at 305 and Lily Nellans at 212, with Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry elected to the vice presidencies. Students ratified all six referendums, making the SAVES, MyCampusToo and Sustainability committees permanent, lowering the GPA requirement to 2.0, creating regional campus ambassadors and requiring more accessible executive discretionary spending reports.

Three films were scheduled at 5:30 p.m.: "The Dark Side of Chocolate" on 22 February, "Chasing Coral" on 22 March and "Bag It" on 19 April, the night of the Earth Day Festival. The money paid for posters and popcorn.

$50 for posters and popcorn

7 February 2018

SGA members rally in Frankfort for higher education

About 20 WKU SGA members joined roughly 100 students from Kentucky's public universities at the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents' annual Rally for Higher Education on the Capitol steps in Frankfort on Feb. 6. Dahmer said the board of student body presidents had been working consistently since August to plan the rally.

Senate backed LGBTQ health curriculum, chair swap on Diversity committee

The senate unanimously passed a resolution supporting integrated LGBTQ health curriculum in WKU's medical education programs, co-authored by diversity and inclusion chair Mark Clark, chief of staff Conner Hounshell and administrative vice president Kara Lowry. Clark was approved as the committee's new chair after Corey Newsome stepped down over scheduling conflicts.

14 February 2018

Senate unanimously backs LGBTQ content in medical education curriculum

A resolution supporting integrated medical education curriculum on lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender health passed unanimously, citing health disparities arising from discrimination and inadequate provider knowledge. It was co-authored by Diversity and Inclusion Chair Mark Clark, Chief of Staff Conner Hounshell and Administrative Vice President Kara Lowry. Clark was also confirmed as Diversity and Inclusion chair after Corey Newsome stepped down.

In the recordHerald, 14 Feb 2018

20 February 2018Festival

Earth Day Festival with the Redshirts and the Treblemakers

Bill 10-18-S allocated $50 from senate discretionary funding to promote the 2018 Earth Day Festival, which the SGA Sustainability Committee held on 19 April from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Local vendors were booked and the entertainment was WKU's own a cappella groups, the Redshirts and the Treblemakers. The bill described the festival as the culmination of the committee's year.

$50 for promotion

SGA funds a $1,200 first-generation student scholarship

Bill 7-18-S passed unanimously, allocating $1,200 to create a scholarship for full-time students whose parents hold no bachelor's degree and who show significant financial need. Co-authors Senator Dallas McKinney and student Olivia Parker were both first-generation students. SGA members and the bill's authors were made ineligible to apply.

In the recordHerald, 21 Feb 2018

28 February 2018

SGA opposes Aramark dining fee rising to $350; new senate seats bill fails 14-18

Resolution 3-18-S passed unanimously, supporting renegotiation of the 20-year Aramark contract signed by Ransdell in March 2017, under which the per-semester dining fee for full-time students not on a meal plan would climb from $75 to $150, then $300, then $350, adding up to $2,800 over four years. Dahmer said the contract was never brought to SGA or the full Board of Regents. A separate bill replacing at-large and graduate seats with first-generation, transfer, non-traditional and ISEC senators failed 14-18 with one abstention.

In the recordHerald, 28 Feb 2018

28 February 2018Lecture

First Campus Safety Panel replaced the safety walk

SGA held its first Campus Safety Panel on the second floor of Downing Student Union on 28 February 2018, with campus officials taking questions from students. Campus improvements chair Garrett Edmonds said he had proposed a panel because it had been too cold to hold a safety walk since he took office. Parking director Jennifer Tougas was among the panelists; President Andi Dahmer asked what could be done about hate crimes on campus, and Chief Diversity Officer Lynne Holland answered that students had to hold each other accountable.

In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2018 - "SGA hosts panel to discuss campus safety"

19 March 2018Lecture

First women in leadership forum drew about twenty people

SGA held its first forum on women in leadership on the evening of 19 March 2018. The panel was Ogden College dean Cheryl Stevens, history professor Patti Minter, faculty regent and former provost Barbara Burch, and Educational Talent Search director Martha Sales, and about 20 students and Bowling Green residents attended. Minter described the psychic energy it took to deal with assumptions about female professors day in and day out. The idea came from the women on SGA's executive board, including Andi Dahmer, Savannah Molyneaux, Kara Lowry and Amy Wyer.

21 March 2018

Lavender Graduation funding passes 28-5 over an unexplained objection

Bill 13-18-S allocated $250 for stoles for the Lavender Recognition Ceremony honoring LGBTQ and ally graduates, passing 28-5. Senator Dallas McKinney spoke against it without giving his reasoning. The same meeting saw Public Relations Chair Will Hurst absent and his seat occupied by vice chair Alex Sergent; asked whether Hurst had been removed, Dahmer said "nothing is official."

In the recordHerald, 21 Mar 2018

26 March 2018

Herald documents a year of escalating internal conflict in SGA

The Herald reported more than 15 proposed constitutional amendments during 2017-18 against about 10 the prior year, alongside longer debates, an emergency judicial council meeting and a walkout by former Public Relations Chair Will Hurst. Dahmer said the year "has become almost toxic in nature" and attributed it to partisan ideology entering a nonpartisan body. Senator Alex Sergent disagreed that the friction was harmful, comparing it to a storm.

In the recordHerald, 26 Mar 2018

28 March 2018

Senator cites Bible verses to explain vote against LGBTQ funding

Senator Dallas McKinney told the senate he had voted against the Lavender Graduation stoles because of "a certain interpretation of the King James Bible," reading verses from Romans; Queer Student Union President Jeremy McFarland walked out during the speech. Senators Noah Moore and Olivia Simpson gave speeches condemning voting on WKU's interests from scripture. A bill to move committee chair appointments to the speaker failed 26-2, with Speaker Ryan Richardson saying "I 100 percent do not support this bill."

In the recordHerald, 28 Mar 2018

3 April 2018

Dahmer announced she would not seek reelection

Citing tension in the senate that she called "almost toxic in nature" and that she attributed to partisan ideology in a body meant to be nonpartisan, Dahmer said in a Facebook post she would not run again and endorsed Conner Hounshell for president alongside Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry, seeking reelection to their executive vice president and administrative vice president seats.

In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2018

3 April 2018

Dahmer declines to seek a second term

Andi Dahmer announced on Facebook that she would not run for re-election as student body president and student regent, and endorsed Conner Hounshell, Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry for the executive board. The announcement followed Herald reporting on months of internal conflict in the senate. Election applications closed the same day, with voting set for April 16 and 17.

In the recordHerald, 3 Apr 2018

4 April 2018

LGBTQ activists address senate after senator's remarks

Several LGBTQ student activists spoke to the senate on April 3 after Senator Dallas McKinney had cited the Bible on March 27, reading verses saying the "wicked" deserved death, as his reason for voting against Bill 13-18-S, which funded $250 for stoles for the Lavender Recognition Ceremony honoring LGBTQ graduates. The bill passed in the senate, and speakers including SGA member Brigid Stakelum and Diversity and Inclusion Committee Chair Mark Clark called the remarks dehumanizing and discriminatory.

In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2018

11 April 2018

Senate votes 28-2 for LGBTQ-friendly housing application questions

A resolution asked Housing and Residence Life to make the sexual orientation and gender identity question optional on housing applications and to add a mandatory question asking whether an applicant is comfortable rooming with an LGBTQ student. Co-author Noah Moore said it would also serve students uncomfortable with an LGBTQ roommate, and noted WKU stood at 2 out of 5 on the Campus Pride Index. The senate also unanimously renamed the ESL international student senator seat to international student senator.

In the recordHerald, 11 Apr 2018

17 April 2018

Judicial Council disqualifies two campaigns mid-election over a Pepe the Frog meme

In an emergency meeting the Judicial Council disqualified the Mayer-Edmonds-Anderson presidential ticket and senate candidate Anna McAvoy for using a Pepe the Frog image in campaign chalkings, finding a violation of election code 3.4.10.1, and suspended Kenan Mujkanovic's campaign for a separate violation. Chief Justice Annalicia Carlson said Garrett Edmonds had been told the image was a hate symbol and chose not to remove it. The MEA campaign called it a "secret meeting"; Carlson said it had been advertised to those involved.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2018

18 April 2018

Mayer wins presidency after disqualification reversed

Stephen Mayer was elected SGA president and student regent, with Garrett Edmonds as executive vice president and Harper Anderson as administrative vice president. Their MEA ticket had been disqualified on April 16 after a complaint over a Pepe the Frog meme in a campaign chalk drawing, but the Judicial Council reversed the disqualification to a suspension before results were announced. Mayer won 35 percent of the 2,378 votes cast in the presidential race, ahead of Conner Hounshell with 33 percent and Kenan Mujkanovic with 32 percent.

In the recordHerald, 18 Apr 2018

24 April 2018

Dahmer details months of harassment

In a Herald investigation, Dahmer said members of SGA had cursed at her, called her derogatory names and exchanged group messages in a GroupMe called the "Justice Friends" wishing her harm over the fall and spring semesters, and that a profane note left on her car on Feb. 9 led her to file a WKU police report and avoid her residence hall for two weeks. Her case was reported to WKU's Title IX office, which told her the conduct did not meet the legal standard for harassment, and it was processed instead by the Office of Student Conduct, which issued no-contact orders against two senators.

In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2018

25 April 2018

Outgoing executives describe the year as 'absolute hell'

In their final officer reports, Executive Vice President Savannah Molyneaux called the year "awful" and an "absolute hell" and said sexism and misogyny persisted in the senate, citing the threatening note left on Dahmer's car and derogatory names used in the SGA offices. She also denied the board opposed Greek life, noting she was president of Sigma Kappa. Director of Public Relations Amy Wyer disclosed that she had become "a statistic, a victim and a survivor" during the year.

In the recordHerald, 25 Apr 2018

May 2018

Caboni announced Title IX review after Dahmer harassment report

University president Timothy Caboni said he would convene a faculty-staff-student committee, co-chaired by sociology professor Lauren McClain and counseling official Karl Laves, to review WKU's Title IX, Equal Employment Opportunity and Office of Student Conduct processes following the Herald's report on the harassment Dahmer said she experienced. President-elect Stephen Mayer called Dahmer "a super strong woman" and said he did not stand for harassment or sexual assault.

In the recordHerald, 1 May 2018

Stephen Mayer (president)

4 September 2018

Former SGA president sues WKU, Caboni and two administrators

Andi Dahmer filed suit against WKU, President Timothy Caboni, Assistant General Counsel Andrea Anderson and Director of Student Activities Charley Pride, citing verbal, mental and emotional abuse and alleging sex discrimination and failure to follow the university's Discrimination and Harassment Policy. The university called the allegations "maliciously untrue" and said it would vigorously defend the claims. WKU said its Title IX office found no Title IX violation but did find Student Code of Conduct violations, for which students were sanctioned.

In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2018

11 September 2018

Senate rejected first Judicial Council nominee of the term

The senate voted 8-7-1 against confirming Wood Brown, a Pike fraternity member and law clerk, as associate justice of the Judicial Council, after Mayer said his constitutional duty required him to appoint whom he judged best despite recusing himself from the interview process; senators argued the Judicial Council's own top-ranked applicant, not Brown, should have been chosen. Mayer's next nominee, Alex Rivera, was confirmed the following week.

In the recordSGA Senate meeting minutes, 11 Sep 2018

14 September 2018

Senate votes down both of the new president's executive nominees

Stephen Mayer's nominees were rejected in his first confirmation votes: Wood Brown for associate justice failed 8-7 with one abstention and one exemption, and Anna McAvoy for director of academic and student affairs failed 6-9, both short of the required two-thirds. Senators questioned Mayer's ability to judge candidates when he had been sequestered from the Judicial Council's interviews. The 2018-19 budget of $100,000, a $15,000 reduction from the prior year, passed 13-4.

In the recordHerald, 14 Sep 2018

20 September 2018

Senate asked WKU to cancel classes on Election Day

SGA unanimously passed Resolution 5-18-F asking the university to cancel classes on Nov. 6, 2018, so students could get to the polls, after a presentation by Francis Wilson of the get-out-the-vote campaign Reg 2 Vote, and approved $300 in support through Bill 7-18-F. The senate also passed Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, which asked WKU to strike code-of-conduct language barring students from refusing a direction from a university official and from audio recording student-faculty meetings. Mayer's nominee Alex Rivera was confirmed as associate justice of the Judicial Council 12-3 after an earlier nomination had failed.

In the recordHerald, 20 Sep 2018

20 September 2018

Senate asks WKU to cancel classes on Election Day and to let students record meetings

Resolution 5-18-F, urging cancellation of classes for the Nov. 6 midterms, passed 15-0 alongside Bill 7-18-F giving $300 to the Reg 2 Vote campaign. Student Francis Wilson told senators that of 290,000 Kentucky students registered in 2016, only about 13 percent voted. Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, seeking removal of Student Code of Conduct clauses requiring compliance with university officials and banning audio recording of student-faculty meetings, both passed 14-0.

In the recordHerald, 20 Sep 2018

23 September 2018

WKU denies Dahmer's claims in court filing

WKU filed its response on Sept. 19 denying that Dahmer suffered a hostile educational environment or sexual harassment during her presidency, and stating she never reported to the Office of Student Conduct or the Title IX coordinator but instead told her residence hall director, who triggered the investigation. The university said the investigation found Student Code of Conduct violations by certain SGA members, who were sanctioned. It argued the GroupMe messages were never intended for Dahmer and so caused her no harm. Dahmer is seeking $75,000 in damages.

In the recordHerald, 23 Sep 2018

25 September 2018

Academic and Student Affairs directorship filled after two failed tries

The senate confirmed Aubrey Kelly as Director of Academic and Student Affairs 24-3-4, three weeks into the term. Initial nominee Ashley Cox was not confirmed at the first meeting after senators questioned her committee attendance, then withdrew when a family member was hospitalized; her replacement, Anna McAvoy, failed confirmation 6-9-1 on Sept. 11 after a senator raised concerns about her scholarship-grading experience.

Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds presented plans for a freshman First Year Village of two new pod-style residence halls at the bottom of the Hill, replacing Bemis Lawrence and Barnes-Campbell halls on the site of the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot. The senate also approved Bill 6-18-F, funding a sustainability film festival, by a 21-4 vote with one abstention.

Author Amy Wyer, herself a member of Alpha Gamma Delta, cited the University of Alabama's Machine coalition and said only one non-Greek member had been elected to that student government since 1914, warning "I fear we have the potential to move in this direction." Former senator Alex Sargent argued against telling students who pay the same tuition that their social needs matter less. A motion to table failed 21-14, short of two-thirds.

24 October 2018

Senate creates a recurring $2,000 first-generation scholarship

A bill by Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr establishing a $2,000 scholarship awarded once per academic year to first-generation students passed 31-1. The Herald cited a 2017 WKU Fact Book study finding an estimated 34.8 percent of first-year, first-time students in fall 2016 were first-generation. Two organizational aid bills also passed, including $1,400 split among Delta Sigma Theta, Phi Beta Sigma and the jump rope club.

Bill 18-18-F, allocating $1,000 to stock a used-textbook library for Colonnade courses in the SGA offices, was tabled 24-3 with one abstention after debate over funding and over whether the collection would stay current as Colonnade courses change. Senator Amy Wyer asked why the WKU Bookstore was "making us buy books they can't resell." Two bylaw amendments passed the same night, one adding flexibility in appointing regional ambassadors and one adding protection against discrimination on the basis of gender identity.

Resolution 7-18-F, written by Diversity and Inclusion Chair Mark Clark in response to reports that the Trump administration was considering narrowly redefining sex, pledged to preserve and improve protections for transgender and nonconforming students regardless of federal action. It passed 30-0. Resolution 8-18-F requiring all new campus buildings to meet LEED standards passed 29-0, and Bill 23-18-F tightening executive board appointments to require a two-thirds senate vote passed 28-1.

President Stephen Mayer's nomination of graduate student Emily Anne Pride, daughter of a former SGA adviser, to a vacated senate seat sparked about 90 minutes of debate before she was confirmed 17-9 with two abstentions. The senate then passed Resolution 10-18-F, supporting denouncement of the white nationalist group Identity Evropa and its attempts to recruit on campus, 28-0, and allocated $430 to the Black Leadership Academic Conference through Bill 24-18-F.

Ninety-minute fight over a nominee; senate denounces Identity Evropa

Mayer's nomination of graduate student Emily Anne Pride, daughter of former SGA adviser Charley Pride, produced roughly an hour and a half of debate before she was confirmed 17-9 with two abstentions; a motion to table failed 8-19-1. Senator Kara Lowry opposed her over her work on Braxton Powell's earlier presidential campaign. Resolution 10-18-F, denouncing Identity Evropa's attempts to recruit on campus, passed 28-0.

SGA opened the spring semester with vacant seats after nine senators were required to step down from their positions. Mayer presented a slate of nominees to fill them, to be voted on the following week. No new legislation was introduced at the meeting.

Study abroad scholarship bill pulled after five competing motions

Bill 2-19-S, which would have barred students who had already received an SGA study abroad scholarship from reapplying, was pulled from the agenda after debate produced five motions ranging from amendments to a 30-second cap on further speeches. The senate also allocated $1,000 to send the Mock Trial team to a national tournament.

27 February 2019

Senate votes 29-1 to move the Confederate capital marker

Resolution 1-19-S, written by senators Kara Lowry, Conner Hounshell and Symone Whalin, called the marker near the Kentucky Museum identifying Bowling Green as the Confederate capital of Kentucky a reminder of oppression, and passed 29-1 with one abstention. An amendment during the meeting changed the ask from removal to relocation into a museum display. Lowry said that was "a good compromise for people who believe that [the marker] is preserving history." Mayer said the resolution would go to the Administrative Council rather than the University Senate.

A week after Snyder's sudden resignation, the senate passed Resolution 4-19-S by a 30-2 vote, calling on top university officials to provide explanations for major decisions. Resolution 4-19-S, passed 30-2 a week after Potter College Dean Larry Snyder resigned abruptly, said top university officials must explain such decisions and implement them in a manner that protects the dignity of those involved. Mayer's renomination of Wood Brown to the Judicial Council was struck down 17-11, short of two-thirds, after Associate Justice Annalicia Carlson said the council preferred Erika Puhakka. After Snyder was asked to resign as Potter College dean on March 26, protests from faculty, staff and students led the University Senate to an unprecedented vote of no confidence in Provost Terry Ballman on April 4, and she resigned the next day. Ogden dean Cheryl Stevens was named acting provost, and days later the Comprehensive Academic Program Evaluation committee recommended suspending 101 of WKU's 380 academic programs.

17 April 2019

Harris-led WGK ticket wins SGA executive election

The WGK ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, with Harris defeating Asha McWilliams for student body president. Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president and Mujkanovic defeated Symone Whalin for administrative vice president. Results were announced at SGA's election party, with the new officers set to take office at the annual banquet; the Herald's results story reported no turnout figures.

In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2019

4 September 2019

First meeting of the year confirms five executive appointments

At its first official meeting of the semester, the senate confirmed all five of President Will Harris's executive branch nominees: Aubrey Kelley as chief of staff, Ashlynn Evans as chief of public relations, Abbey Norvell as director of academic and student affairs, Paul Brosky as director of information technology and Josh Zaczek as Legislative Research Committee chair. Appointees outlined plans including wider use of counseling center fee vouchers and a revival of the need-based Earn-a-Computer program.

In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2019

10 September 2019Programme

Greeks Go Green sustainability contest funded at $75

Bill 1-19-F allocated $75 from senate discretionary funding for prizes in Greeks Go Green, a competition between WKU's Greek organisations to run the most sustainable chapter house by logging environmentally friendly actions for points. The contest ran from 20 September 2019 through April, with winners announced at the Greek Week convocation. The bill passed its second reading on 10 September 2019.

$75

In the recordSGA Bill 1-19-F, Funding for Greeks Go Green

11 September 2019

Senate blocks budget over special projects fund

The senate refused to pass the year's budget over a $6,500 special projects fund the executive branch wanted for a sand volleyball court and hammock space at the First Year Village green space. Senators including Anthony Survance objected that the allocation cut into scholarship money, with Survance calling the motion "slimy", and the senate voted to keep $3,000 in its discretionary fund and $35,000 in scholarships. The executive branch pulled the budget, forcing a week's wait before a revised version could be voted on.

In the recordHerald, 11 Sep 2019

11 September 2019

SGA deadlocks over budget, executive branch pulls the bill

The senate and executive branch failed to pass a budget at their second meeting, splitting over a $6,500 special projects allocation for a sand volleyball court and hammock spaces at the First Year Village. Senator Anthony Survance called the motion "slimy" and said it cut money reserved for scholarships; the senate voted to keep $3,000 in its own discretionary fund and $35,000 in scholarships, and the executive branch withdrew the budget. Rules required a full week before a revised budget could be voted on.

In the recordHerald, 11 Sep 2019

19 September 2019

Budget passes unanimously with spending stipulations

All 13 senators approved the yearly budget after a compromise added stipulations restricting the special projects fund to the First Year Village plans and redistributing any money unspent by March 3 back to discretionary and voucher funds. The budget's passage let Bills 1-19-F (Greeks Go Green) and 2-19-F (funding for Bowling Green Pride) pass unanimously. The senate also amended its election codes to halve campaign spending maximums, which had been $300 for presidential candidates, $125 for vice presidential candidates and $50 for senate candidates.

In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2019

19 September 2019

Budget passes with spending stipulations; senate halves campaign spending caps

All 13 senators approved the budget after a three-part stipulation confined the special projects fund to First Year Village plans and set a March 3 reversion formula. The senate also halved election code campaign maximums, previously $300 for president, $125 for the vice presidencies and $50 for senators, over objections from Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds, who called SGA turnout "awful" and estimated 1,500 students voted the previous year. Senator Symone Whalin said poorer students were less likely to run for executive office.

In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2019

2 October 2019

Senate votes 17-15 to cancel a meeting for a sorority philanthropy event

A motion by Senator Hope Wells to cancel the Oct. 8 senate meeting for Kappa Delta's Shenanigans passed 17-15 after debate. Senator Anthony Survance argued that given recent controversies with Greek organizations SGA should not signal endorsement, while Senator Brigid Stakelum said the reason was practical, that quorum might not be met. Newly elected senators were sworn in at the same meeting by Chief Justice Isaac Keller.

In the recordHerald, 2 Oct 2019

8 October 2019

Two SGA members organize protest against Alpha Xi Delta

Senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance organized a protest at the Shenanigans philanthropy event in response to a Twitter video showing WKU Alpha Xi Delta members singing a racial slur. Survance said the vote to cancel the senate meeting for the event helped prompt the protest, and the pair created a Facebook group titled "Demand Alpha Xi Delta's Removal." Whalin said administrative inaction signaled that minority students were not a priority.

In the recordHerald, 8 Oct 2019

24 October 2019

Senate passes Resolution 4-19-F against Alpha Xi Delta

The senate voted 24-7 to pass Resolution 4-19-F, authored by senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance, supporting disciplinary action up to suspension from Greek affairs against the Epsilon Kappa chapter of Alpha Xi Delta. The resolution followed an August Twitter video showing AXiD members singing a racial slur in a rap song, and the authors said administrative silence signaled the university did not care about minority students. Before passage the senate amended the title to drop a call for outright removal from campus.

In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2019

24 October 2019

Senate passes Resolution 4-19-F seeking discipline against Alpha Xi Delta, 24-7

After a motion stripped "Removal from Campus" from the title and a friendly amendment substituted "Suspension from Greek Affairs," the senate passed the resolution 24-7. Authors Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance said they wanted more than "an article from the Herald or an email from Bob Skipper." Senator Mary Mayo said it was not SGA's job to act as a disciplinary committee; the resolution was to be submitted to the Faculty Senate.

In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2019

30 October 2019

Executive board veto of Resolution 4-19-F upheld

The executive board vetoed Resolution 4-19-F by a 4-0 vote with two abstentions, and the senate confirmed the veto at its Tuesday meeting. President Will Harris, one of the abstainers, said the resolution's discrimination claim would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and no violation had been noted by the Office of Student Conduct, while co-author Anthony Survance accused the executive branch of dragging the issue out. Senators also raised Harris's connection to Alpha Xi Delta as one of its knights, which he rejected as grounds for bias.

In the recordHerald, 30 Oct 2019

30 October 2019

Executive board vetoes Resolution 4-19-F 4-0; senate sustains the veto

The executive board vetoed the Alpha Xi Delta resolution 4-0 with two of six members abstaining, and the senate confirmed the veto. President Will Harris, who abstained, said the discrimination clause the resolution invoked would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and that the Office of Student Conduct had noted no violation. Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek disputed the reasoning, and Harris was questioned about his status as an Alpha Xi Delta knight.

In the recordHerald, 30 Oct 2019

7 November 2019

Chief justice tells senate the AXiD resolution would be symbolic; student urges labor committee

Chief Justice Isaac Keller told senators the resolution would be purely symbolic because SGA cannot direct WKU to defund an organization on grounds of discrimination, and suggested supporters take the matter to the Title IX office or the Kentucky Human Rights Commission. Harris said no student had filed a formal discrimination charge. Former senator Jay Wells addressed the meeting urging SGA to form a labor committee, citing cut student worker hours and the CAPE committee's recommendation to suspend 101 academic programs.

SGA reports record 398 scholarship applications

Director of Academic and Student Affairs Abbey Norvell reported 398 scholarship applications, including 132 for winter term, 122 for the first generation scholarship, 81 for study abroad, 31 for scholar development, 10 for ISEC and 22 for the revived Earn-a-Computer program. Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds reported First Year Village construction was on schedule and said a remaining building near the old library site would be torn down if incoming student numbers did not require the beds.

Senators quietly leave their seats, two committee chairs vacant

The Herald reported that senators and committee chairs had vacated positions since the fall semester, most leaving to study abroad or over schedule conflicts, weakening the senate's numbers. The SAVES and Sustainability committee chairs were both vacant with no replacements identified, and President Will Harris posted an open SGA application on social media to recruit. The meeting also covered planning for the March Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort.

Go With the Flow feminine hygiene bill passes unanimously

Bill 1-20-S, funding the Go With the Flow program that supplies feminine hygiene products in campus restrooms, passed the senate unanimously. The bill, carried forward by Campus Improvement Chair Matthew Barr, doubled the program's budget from $588, and a floor amendment from Senator Symone Whalin raised the final amount to $1,300 from senate discretionary funds. Products were to be placed in Grise Hall, DSU, Preston Center, Gary Ransdell Hall and Snell Hall, including gender neutral bathrooms.

Bill 2-20-S passed unanimously on 18 February 2020, funding a professional etiquette dinner for students at WKU's Glasgow regional campus and subsidising the ticket price, with Glasgow covering the rest. Executive vice president Garrett Edmonds, who brought the bill, said it was aimed at students from small towns who had never faced a table set with several forks and knives, and that to his knowledge it was the only etiquette dinner held at a WKU regional campus.

Senate approves $5,000 hammocks project

The senate voted to pass Bill 3-20-S, allocating $5,000 from the special projects fund to begin planning hammock poles across campus, after the sand volleyball court proposed earlier in the year was deemed too expensive. Planned locations included spots near most residence halls and the Valley, and Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds said he and Harris ran so SGA would be known for more than "scantrons and greenbooks". 11 March 2020

WKU extends spring break, moves classes online amid COVID-19

WKU announced it would extend spring break by one week and transition to "alternative delivery formats" for classes amid growing coronavirus concerns, with President Tim Caboni recommending that students who could safely return home do so. The announcement came after the University of Kentucky and University of Louisville suspended in-person classes. In-person instruction never resumed that semester, upending the rest of SGA's spring calendar.

20 April 2020

Spring elections postponed until fall as SGA moves to Zoom

With campus closed by COVID-19, SGA postponed its spring elections until at least September so voting could happen in person, and added an "emergency clause" constitutional amendment allowing cabinet terms to be extended until the following election with judicial oversight. The cabinet continued meeting over Zoom every Tuesday. Harris said that after scholarships were awarded, the remainder of SGA's budget would be donated to the WKU Opportunity Fund and Emergency Relief Fund, and SGA gave its remaining food bank goods to the Office of Sustainability for redistribution.

SGA adds constitutional emergency clause and redirects remaining budget to relief funds

President Will Harris said that after scholarships were awarded the remainder of SGA's budget would go to the WKU Opportunity Fund and Emergency Relief Fund. SGA also donated its remaining food bank goods to the Office of Sustainability.

December 2020

WKU relented and allowed pass grades after SGA's P/D/F campaign

Provost Cheryl Stevens told faculty that students who faced COVID-related problems could opt for a pass grade instead of a B or C, reversing the university's earlier refusal. The Faculty Senate had voted 40-9 in favor and SGA voted unanimously for the option, presenting nearly 20 pages of student testimony; SGA's petition had drawn over 3,500 signatures in three days. Students had to email their professor by Jan. 13, with the final decision left to the faculty member.

6 November 2024

Three senators removed from the Senate after second censure

The Judicial Council voted 7-0 to remove Malick Ibrahim, Myricle Gholston and Karisha Petty for excessive unexcused absences, each having accumulated at least six. Section 2.2 of the bylaws allows three unexcused absences a semester, and Section 4.6.12 of the constitution requires removal after a second censure; all three had already been censured once and given extra office hours. The council's minutes said senators cannot represent students they are not present to serve. Petty later told the Herald her absences were due to medical issues.

The Judicial Council voted 7-0 to remove them under a constitutional provision requiring removal of any senator censured twice, calling the decision a matter of accountability rather than an attack on character.

General counsel tells SGA that House Bill 4 binds its spending

WKU General Counsel Andrea Anderson told the Senate that the WKU Pride Center would become a student-run organization, losing its status as a university-related initiative and its Downing Student Union office, under House Bill 4. Anderson said the statute, passed March 28 and enforced by the Attorney General's office and a committee formed by Provost Bud Fischer, applies to SGA because SGA receives university money for events and bills. She said SGA could still fund organizations and events if they were content neutral, and that HB4 counts social media and digital content as a resource.

11 May 2026

Lucas named ODK Circle Leader of the Year

WKU's Omicron Delta Kappa circle named President Caden Lucas its Heather Strode Circle Leader of the Year, an award for a student demonstrating leadership and dedication to the campus community across ODK's five core values.

2 June 2026

Lucas voices concern over proposed tuition increase

WKU released a proposed 2026-27 budget that would raise tuition by $210 to $6,246 per semester within a $405.1 million operating plan. Lucas, identified as SGA president and soon-to-be student regent, said he was "generally concerned" by a proposal that would raise the cost of attending WKU. He said students deserved both a high-quality education and an affordable way to achieve it.

In the recordHerald, 2 Jun 2026

5 June 2026

Robinson cast the lone dissenting vote on a tuition increase

At his last meeting as student regent, Robinson voted against a $204, 1.69 percent tuition increase that the rest of the Board of Regents approved, saying the board had to do everything it could to preserve affordability.

In the recordHerald, 5 Jun 2026

5 June 2026

Regents approve tuition increase over student regent's lone no vote

The Board of Regents approved a $204 tuition increase to $6,240 per semester, the sixth consecutive yearly increase, along with a 5% housing rate increase and a 2% meal plan increase as part of a $405 million operating budget. Every regent voted in favor except outgoing SGA president Rush Robinson, casting his final vote as student regent before Lucas took the seat. The board also suspended several majors, including kinesiology and geological sciences, for reworking and mergers.

In the recordHerald, 5 Jun 2026

7 July 2026

SGA gains a new adviser as Rash becomes interim director

Andrew Rash, who had served as Associate Director of Student Activities and Greek Life since August 2022 and as SGA's faculty adviser, became interim director of Student Activities on July 1 following the retirement of Charley Pride. Assistant Director of Student Activities and Leadership and Volunteerism Amelia Kolb will advise SGA going forward. Rash said his new duties cover budgeting and Downing Student Union management.

In the recordHerald, 7 Jul 2026

7 July 2026

SGA got a new adviser in Student Activities leadership change

Andrew Rash, who had served as SGA's faculty adviser and Associate Director of Student Activities and Greek Life since 2022, became interim director of the Department of Student Activities on July 1 following the retirement of longtime director Charley Pride. Assistant Director of Student Activities and Leadership and Volunteerism Amelia Kolb took over as SGA's adviser going forward.

8 April 2026

Executive candidates face off at SGA town hall

SGA held a town hall in the Downing Student Union Auditorium for the two executive tickets: Caden Lucas with Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry, and Jaden Marshall with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling moderated as the candidates answered 27 questions submitted by students. Both tickets made increasing awareness of SGA operations and outreach to the student body their central campaign promise.

9 April 2026

Herald and Revolution Radio hosted a presidential debate

College Heights Herald Editor-in-Chief Jake McMahon and Assistant News Editor Kane Smith sat down with presidential candidates Caden Lucas and Jaden Marshall for a debate co-hosted with campus station Revolution Radio, ahead of voting opening the following Monday on TopNet.

In the recordHerald, 9 Apr 2026

15 April 2026

Caden Lucas wins SGA presidential election

Caden Lucas and his ticket of Vice President-elect Jakob Barker and Chief Financial Officer-elect Will Derryberry won the spring election to serve during the 2026-27 academic year, defeating Jaden Marshall's ticket. Lucas, a junior senator, WKU Spiritmaster and chairman of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition, ran on the motto "Lead, build, deliver" and a promise to make SGA operations more visible to students. The Herald did not publish vote totals or turnout figures; the story also listed the full slate of senators elected to the incoming 26th Senate.

In the recordHerald, 15 Apr 2026

24 April 2026

Lucas named a 2026 Truman Scholar

Days after taking SGA's top office, President Caden Lucas was named a 2026 Truman Scholar, WKU's second in the scholarship's history and Kentucky's only recipient that year. The award, chosen from 781 candidates at 305 colleges nationally, provides $30,000 toward graduate or professional study and recognizes commitment to public service.

In the recordWKU News, 24 Apr 2026

28 April 2026

26th Senate seated; tie vote for speaker resolved in Butler's favor

At the first meeting of the 26th Senate, outgoing president Rush Robinson passed the traditional red suit jacket to Caden Lucas, and the body swore in Gabi Pace as chief of staff, Cayden Bailey as chief communications officer, Maggie Phelps to the judicial council and defeated presidential candidate Jaden Marshall as an at-large senator. The race for speaker of the senate ended in a 9-9 tie between Amelia Tucker and Veronica Butler, and Chief Justice Sophie Sterling confirmed that neither the constitution nor the bylaws addressed a tie. Outgoing speaker Hadley Whipple ordered a re-vote, which elected Butler as speaker.

What this is

A year-by-year record of student government at Western Kentucky University, from the ratification of the Associated Students constitution in April 1966 to the present. Every entry names the source it came from.

Corrections

The names here start with the plaque in the SGA Chambers, and the plaque is known to be wrong in places. Where the archive disagrees with it, this site follows the archive and records the change on the corrections page. If you served, or you know that a year here is wrong, the project wants to hear from you through the Student Government Association office.

Reuse

Text on this site is the work of the project. Photographs, documents and legislation are reproduced from Western Kentucky University's own open archives and from the College Heights Herald and the Talisman; each item names the collection, issue and page it came from and links to the original.

Built 5 August 2026. The whole record is readable as data: years.json. Method and scope are set out on the about page.
